signals.topic: hookify action:warn double-fires on PreToolUse and PostToolUse for the same tool call
signals.summary: hookify rules with action:warn and event:all fire twice per tool invocation — once in PreToolUse and once in PostToolUse — because pretooluse.py and posttooluse.py share identical rule-loading logic with no phase filtering. Users see duplicate systemMessage warnings for every matching tool.
signals.review_reason: User-reported confirmed double-fire causes repeated redundant warnings on every matching tool call, degrading UX noticeably. The workaround (using tool-specific event instead of event:all) is available. P2 because it's a single report and the impact is annoyance rather than functional block.

source_issues.title: [hookify] Feature Request: Add hook_phase field to control PreToolUse vs PostToolUse triggering
source_issues.evidence: action:warn rules fire twice per single tool call — once PreToolUse, once PostToolUse. Confirmed reproducible by the issue author. The double-trigger is a direct UX degradation that worsens with frequent tool use.

signals.topic: ralph-loop Stop hook crosses session boundaries and hijacks unrelated Claude Code sessions in the same project
signals.summary: The Stop hook in ralph-loop fires in sessions other than the one that started the loop because a state file without session_id falls through the isolation check. Users see loop feedback injected into unrelated conversations, corrupting them and distorting the progress signal.
aliases: ralph loop stop hook fires in wrong session
signals.review_reason: Cross-session bleed is a session isolation failure that actively corrupts unrelated Claude Code sessions by injecting loop feedback into them. Hit by two independent sessions simultaneously, with confirmed root cause. Non-blocking in that Claude Code still runs, but the UX corruption of unrelated sessions is severe.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: cross-session Stop hook bleed when session_id is empty in state file
source_issues.evidence: Hit independently by two distinct sessions on 2026-05-08 in the same project. State file showed iteration:216 with no concrete progress — the hook fired in every session on every model stop with identical content. Root cause confirmed in stop-hook.sh isolation logic.

signals.topic: fakechat MCP server outlives Claude Code and orphan-holds port 8787, blocking reconnection
signals.summary: fakechat's bun server does not self-terminate when Claude Code exits abnormally. The orphaned process holds the FAKECHAT_PORT port, causing EADDRINUSE on the next session and a silent 'failed to reconnect' error with no actionable hint about the orphan.
aliases: fakechat server does not shutdown on parent exit
signals.review_reason: Orphan-hold causes total fakechat channel failure on reconnection — a blocking workflow interruption with an opaque error message that doesn't point to the root cause. Users must manually find and kill the old bun process to recover. Clear reproduction steps and root cause identified.

source_issues.title: fakechat MCP server can outlive Claude Code and orphan-hold its port
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible by force-killing Claude Code and attempting to start a new session. User sees 'Failed to reconnect to plugin:fakechat:fakechat' with no indication the cause is a lingering bun process. Bun.serve() keeps the event loop alive after stdin EOF with no signal handler.

signals.topic: Context7 plugin MCP server silently fails to load — plugin appears enabled but mcp__context7__ tools never appear
signals.summary: The Context7 plugin's .mcp.json lacks the required 'mcpServers' wrapper key, causing Claude Code to silently ignore the MCP server entry. The plugin shows as enabled and skills load, but all Context7 tools are absent with no error, warning, or log entry.
aliases: context7 mcpServers wrapper missing schema mismatch
signals.review_reason: Complete silent failure of Context7 MCP functionality with zero user-facing feedback. The plugin appears enabled but its core value — mcp__context7__ tools for live documentation — is entirely absent. Users have no diagnostic path without manually inspecting the .mcp.json file. High confidence due to reproducible steps and cross-platform confirmation.

source_issues.title: Context7 plugin's .mcp.json missing 'mcpServers' wrapper — silent load failure
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps provided: enable plugin, list available MCP tools — mcp__context7__ tools absent. Manual addition of mcpServers wrapper fixes it. All other marketplace plugins (telegram, figma, stripe, supabase, postman, fakechat, discord) use the correct schema. Confirmed across Windows and npm-installed Claude Code versions.

signals.topic: skill-creator run_eval.py parallel mode produces ~1/N recall regardless of description quality, making parallel eval results unreliable
signals.summary: run_eval.py uses a shared .claude/commands/ directory across all parallel workers, so each worker's subprocess sees all N synthetic command files and picks a sibling instead of its own. A description that triggers 100% serially scores ~10% with default 10 workers, corrupting all evaluation results.
aliases: skill creator eval harness shared commands directory
signals.review_reason: Parallel mode produces systematically wrong evaluation results — recall is 10x lower than reality. This directly causes skill creators to abandon or degrade working descriptions based on false negative eval data. The workaround (--num-workers 1) works but defeats the purpose of parallelization. Empirical reproduction with clear root cause.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_eval.py parallel workers cross-pollinate, producing ~1/N recall regardless of description quality
source_issues.evidence: Same description and eval set on same machine: 11% recall with 10 workers vs 100% recall with 1 worker. Root cause identified in source: all workers write to shared .claude/commands/, each subprocess sees all N files, and detection only matches the specific worker's UUID. Workaround: --num-workers 1.

signals.topic: Plugin loader loads all skills from repository instead of respecting marketplace.json declarations
signals.summary: When installing plugins (document-skills, example-skills) via /plugin install, the loader installs all ~17 skills from the repo instead of only the subset declared in marketplace.json. This causes duplicate skills (wasting ~50k tokens of context), namespace pollution, and makes the context window less usable for actual work.
aliases: plugin loads all skills instead of declared subset
document-skills installs all 17 skills instead of 4
signals.review_reason: Two independent reporters confirm the same root cause: plugin loader ignores marketplace.json declarations. User impact is explicit — ~50k tokens wasted on duplicate skills, context window polluted with 17 skills instead of 4, actual work capacity reduced. Not P0 because count=2 (<3) and the issue affects the skills library packaging layer rather than a core Claude Code main-flow.

source_issues.title: document-skills plugin loads all skills from repo instead of only declared ones in marketplace.json
source_issues.evidence: Plugin declares 4 skills in marketplace.json but loads all 17 skills. Extra 13 skills pollute namespace and waste context.

source_issues.title: document-skills and example-skills plugins install identical content, causing duplicate skills
source_issues.evidence: Both plugins install identical all-17-skills content. ~50k wasted tokens on duplicate definitions. Skills like pptx (6.3k tokens) appear twice in /context. User-impact: context window bloat reduces available space for actual work.

signals.topic: npx skills add installs to wrong directory (~/.agents/skills/) — skills invisible to Claude Code
signals.summary: Skills installed via npx skills add are placed in ~/.agents/skills/, but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills for available skills. Users end up with skills that cannot be used.
signals.review_reason: Single reporter. The installation path mismatch causes skills to be silently installed but completely unusable — key functionality blocked for users relying on npx-based skill installation. Downgraded to P2 due to count=1 and single-repo impact.

source_issues.title: npx skills add may install skills to ~/.agents/skills/, but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills
source_issues.evidence: npx skills add installs skills to ~/.agents/skills/ but Claude Code only scans ~/.claude/skills. Skills are silently installed but unusable.

signals.topic: MCP returns uncompressed excess data — causes context congestion with large datasets
signals.summary: When MCP servers return large datasets (e.g., database queries), Claude Code via MCP does not compress or paginate the data, causing context congestion and degraded performance.
aliases: MCP large response causes context overflow
signals.review_reason: Single reporter. The issue describes a real workflow degradation when using database-related MCP servers — large responses congest the context window. However count=1 and it's framed as an optimization question rather than a confirmed breakage. Kept because context congestion is a concrete user-impact scenario.

source_issues.title: MCP returns excess data
source_issues.evidence: User reports that MCP data is not compressed; large database MCP returns cause context congestion. Explicitly asks for an engineering optimization.

signals.topic: skill-creator eval-viewer cannot find per-eval eval_metadata.json — shows 'No prompt found' for every run
signals.summary: eval-viewer/generate_review.py looks for eval_metadata.json at the wrong directory depth (run_dir/ and run_dir.parent/) while the SKILL.md instructions place it at the eval directory level. Every run renders '(No prompt found)', making the eval-viewer tool effectively broken for its intended purpose.
signals.review_reason: Single reporter with a precise, reproducible bug. The eval-viewer tool is a core part of skill-creator for evaluating skill quality — it silently returns '(No prompt found)' for every run, making it unusable without a manual workaround. Downgraded to P2 due to count=1 and the workaround exists.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: eval-viewer doesn't find per-eval metadata
source_issues.evidence: generate_review.py checks run_dir/eval_metadata.json and run_dir.parent/eval_metadata.json but SKILL.md places the file at eval_dir/eval_metadata.json (two levels up). Every run shows '(No prompt found)'. Workaround: manually copy the file to each run-1/ directory.

signals.topic: Queued message Send/Interrupt permanently deletes user input instead of processing it
signals.summary: When a user queues a message during active Goose processing and clicks the Send button to interject, the current task stops correctly but the queued message itself is silently deleted — never added to conversation history, never sent to the LLM, and never recoverable. Users must retype the message. This is 100% reproducible on every interjection attempt.
aliases: Message removed from queue but never sent
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports both confirming 100% reproducible message loss on interjection. The Send button is documented to interrupt and process the interjected message, but instead permanently deletes user input. This is a clear data-loss bug that directly violates the documented feature contract. Both reports are from Desktop UI users on separate machines with fresh installs, ruling out local corruption.

source_issues.title: Queued message lost when clicking Send — message removed from queue but never added to conversation history
source_issues.evidence: Clicking Send on queued message stops the current task (interrupt works) but the message payload is dropped rather than injected into conversation. Message disappears entirely — not in DB, not in session context. Goose docs confirm Send should interrupt and then process the interjected message. User must retype. Closed as fixed.

source_issues.title: Queued message interrupt kills processing and deletes the queued message
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible. Every interjection attempt: current response cut off mid-stream, queued message deleted, never delivered. Confirmed across fresh macOS reinstall + fresh Goose install. 1 comment confirms same pattern. Closed as fixed.

signals.topic: MCP extension timeout config ignored on Linux — streamable_http and stdio transports capped at ~30s TCP_USER_TIMEOUT
signals.summary: Long-running MCP tool calls fail on Linux after ~30 seconds even when the extension is configured with a much longer timeout (e.g., timeout: 300). The reqwest HTTP client is built without applying the resolved extension timeout, and Linux TCP_USER_TIMEOUT defaults to ~30s, causing premature connection resets for legitimate long-running tools like cargo build, cargo test, or Elastic Agent Builder.
aliases: reqwest socket TCP_USER_TIMEOUT resets MCP calls
Extension timeout config not applied to HTTP client
signals.review_reason: Two issues with distinct transport types (stdio and streamable_http) that share the same root cause pattern: extension timeout is not applied to the underlying reqwest HTTP client on Linux, causing TCP_USER_TIMEOUT to prematurely terminate long-running MCP tool calls. Issue 9100 was closed fixed for the session snapshot path; issue 9022 confirms the same problem persists for streamable_http transport. Long-running MCP tools (cargo build/test, Elastic Agent Builder) are a core use case for Goose.

source_issues.title: stdio extension timeout in config.yaml is ignored -- session snapshot always persists 30s default
source_issues.evidence: Config timeout:300 set in config.yaml; fresh sessions snapshot timeout:30. Verified across 200+ sessions. MCP tool calls (cargo test, cargo build) fail with -32603: request timeout after PT30S despite 300s config. Root cause: persist_extension_state uses Extension.config from session snapshot (timeout:30) rather than config.yaml. Closed as fixed.

source_issues.title: Streamable HTTP MCP calls on Linux may reset after ~30s despite larger extension timeout
source_issues.evidence: Elastic Agent Builder MCP tools that take >30s server-side cause client connection reset at ~30s. Root cause: reqwest::Client built without resolved extension timeout, and Linux TCP_USER_TIMEOUT defaults to ~30s. Confirmed by tracing create_streamable_http_client. Affects streamable_http transport. Open issue.

signals.topic: Session silently hangs after chat-mode tool-call interception with permanent message loss
signals.summary: When Goose intercepts a tool call in chat mode and returns a text-only summary, the session's agentic loop terminates with no error surfaced to the user. User messages sent during the hang are accepted by the UI but never persisted to the database — they are silently dropped. Users experience sessions appearing alive but completely unresponsive for 40+ minutes with no indication of failure.
aliases: Messages disappear from UI during session hang
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow blocker: the agentic loop permanently terminates on a specific chat-mode pattern, the session silently dies with no error surfaced, and user messages are silently lost from both the active queue and the DB. 40+ minutes of unresponsiveness with no UI indication is a severe UX failure. Clear reproduction path, root cause identified (chat mode returns tool_calls:[] with dangling intent text, session agentic loop terminates), and documented across two independent stall events in the same session.

source_issues.title: Session silently hangs after chat-mode response — subsequent user messages receive no response
source_issues.evidence: Session stalls with zero LLM calls for 40 minutes. DB shows user message qyz6gg8r stored with no assistant response following. Message 0nln6fpt visible in UI but absent from DB. Two separate stalls in the same session confirmed; second stall never recovered. No user-visible error or indication. Work task (chatgpt-code-review.sh) never completed.

signals.topic: DeepSeek reasoning_content not passed back to API on multi-turn conversations via OpenAI-compatible providers
signals.summary: DeepSeek models (deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro) fail with HTTP 400 on follow-up turns when used via OpenAI-compatible providers. DeepSeek's thinking mode requires reasoning_content to be passed back in subsequent requests, but Goose does not handle this field, causing the API to reject the conversation.
aliases: DeepSeek thinking mode broken in multi-turn
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn conversations with DeepSeek models are completely broken — every follow-up message returns HTTP 400 and the session becomes unusable. This is not a cosmetic issue; it renders a major model family (DeepSeek v4) non-functional for the primary use case of multi-turn assistance. The bug is clearly traced to Goose not handling the reasoning_content field, with 400 error logs as concrete evidence.

source_issues.title: DeepSeek models via OpenAI-compatible providers fail: reasoning_content not handled
source_issues.evidence: First turn works; second turn fails with Bad request (400): reasoning_content in thinking mode must be passed back to the API. LLM request logs show 'reasoning: true' being sent but reasoning_content from prior response not included in follow-up request. Affects OpenCode Go as provider with DeepSeek models. Workaround: use non-DeepSeek models (GLM-5, Kimi K2.5, Mimo). Open issue.

signals.topic: extra_body/provider-specific request parameters not forwarded to OpenAI-compatible API endpoints
signals.summary: When extra_body is set in recipe settings for OpenAI-compatible providers (e.g., Mistral's reasoning_effort parameter), the configuration is correctly parsed into request_params on ModelConfig but never merged into the actual HTTP request payload sent to the API. Provider-specific parameters are silently dropped.
signals.review_reason: Provider-specific request parameters are silently dropped with no error or warning to the user. Mistral's reasoning_effort controls whether the model uses heavy or light reasoning — without it, the model may behave differently from what the user configured. This is a functional regression: the feature is configured but produces no effect. Logs confirm the parameter reaches ModelConfig but is never merged into the request.

source_issues.title: `extra_body` settings not applied to OpenAI-compatible provider requests
source_issues.evidence: extra_body in recipe YAML parsed correctly into request_params field on ModelConfig. LLM request logs confirm request_params contains reasoning_effort:'high'. Actual API payload does NOT include reasoning_effort. Root cause: create_request in openai.rs builds payload but never merges request_params. Closed as fixed.

signals.topic: Bundle size exceeds platform limits, blocking Stagehand deployment in serverless/edge functions (e.g., Convex)
signals.summary: Stagehand 包体积过大（51.55 MiB > 限制 42.92 MiB），导致无法在 Convex 等 serverless 平台中正常运行，阻断主流程。
signals.review_reason: Single-issue but clear and complete evidence: main workflow completely blocked (cannot deploy Stagehand to Convex), with exact numbers (51.55 MiB vs 42.92 MiB limit) and no available workaround. Not a feature request — this is a functional blocker with concrete platform incompatibility.

source_issues.title: Reduce Bundle Size
source_issues.evidence: User reports bundle size of @browserbasehq/stagehand + playwright-core exceeds Convex's zipped maximum (51.55 MiB > maximum size 42.92 MiB), preventing Stagehand from running within Convex functions at all. No workaround available.

signals.topic: Stagehand v3 storage state persistence completely broken — userDataDir doesn't work, storageState() method missing
signals.summary: Stagehand v3 中 userDataDir 完全不工作（目录从未被创建），storageState() 方法被移除，导致用户无法在会话间持久化认证状态（cookies、localStorage），必须编写手动 workaround 且无法处理 HttpOnly cookies。
signals.review_reason: Core workflow break with detailed evidence: authentication state cannot persist across sessions in v3, blocking automated testing workflows. Workaround exists but is incomplete (misses HttpOnly cookies). Issue is open and actively discussed (7 comments), clearly affecting all v3 users migrating from v2.

source_issues.title: Storage state persistence broken in Stagehand v3 - userDataDir doesn't work, storageState() method missing
source_issues.evidence: userDataDir directory is never created (false after init() and close()); storageState() is not a function on stagehand.context or page.context(); HttpOnly cookies cannot be extracted via workaround; affects all v2→v3 migration users; workaround is functional but not production-ready.

signals.topic: Windows 文件上传功能完全不可用
signals.summary: 在 Windows 平台上，用户上传任何文件（包括图片）均失败，控制台报错，核心文件上传流程阻断。
signals.review_reason: Windows 平台文件上传功能完全阻断，属于核心交互功能失效，用户在 Windows 环境无法完成图片/文件上传操作，count=1 但影响面覆盖整个 Windows 用户群，是明确的主流程阻断问题。

source_issues.title: windows无法上传文件
source_issues.evidence: 聊天时windows无法上传图片，无论上传什么都不成功，附带了错误截图和控制台日志。

signals.topic: 非标准端口部署时 CSRF 认证失败导致登录不可用
signals.summary: nginx 配置中 $host 变量会丢弃端口号，导致默认 2026 端口下 CSRF Origin 校验失败，用户无法登录。
signals.review_reason: 默认部署配置下用户无法登录，属认证主流程阻断。DeerFlow 默认监听 2026 端口，该端口为非标准端口（非 80/443），所有非标准端口部署均受影响。CSRF 校验失败导致认证流程完全不可用，属于 P0 级别。

source_issues.title: docker/nginx/nginx.conf: proxy_set_header Host $host strips port causing CSRF auth failure on non-standard ports
source_issues.evidence: 使用默认 docker-compose 配置（端口 2026）时登录失败，nginx $host 丢弃端口导致 Origin≠Host，CSRF 校验返回 401 Unauthorized。issue 已关闭（修复后），但作为用户痛点记录。

signals.topic: Sandbox 崩溃后 Agent 陷入拒绝连接死循环导致程序退出
signals.summary: Sandbox 内报错导致容器崩溃停止，Agent 陷入 connection refused 死循环，最终程序退出，缺乏自动重启机制。
signals.review_reason: Sandbox 崩溃是运行时常发的可靠性问题，崩溃后无重启机制导致 agent 陷入死循环并最终程序退出，完整工作流被阻断。这是可重现的运行时可靠性缺陷，非边缘场景。

source_issues.title: sandbox重启机制
source_issues.evidence: sandbox 中的报错使镜像崩溃从而 stop container，导致 agent 陷入拒绝连接的死循环，最终程序退出。用户明确请求 sandbox 镜像重启机制。

signals.topic: 新建 Agent 时跳过用户 prompt 直接完成创建，SOUL.md 为空且可能保存到错误目录
signals.summary: 用户在 New Agent 界面输入名字后，系统不等用户输入具体 prompt 内容就完成创建，SOUL.md 文件为空；偶尔停在设计步骤但保存到了 default 目录而非当前用户目录。
signals.review_reason: Agent 创建工作流几乎必现阻断：用户无法完成 prompt 输入导致 SOUL.md 为空，且存在用户隔离缺陷（数据保存到错误用户目录），属于主流程功能缺陷，虽 count=1 但用户影响明确且严重。

source_issues.title: [Bug] 在New Agent时输入名字之后没有等用户prompt具体内容就直接think完后完成Agent 创建
source_issues.evidence: 用户描述几乎必现，SOUL.md 文件为空，且 _current_user 在保存时有时取不到 userid，导致 agent 保存到 default 目录而非登录用户的目录。附截图和代码分析。

signals.topic: EventStore 存储 content 类型不兼容导致 SQLite 写入失败
signals.summary: event_store 存储逻辑只处理了 content 为 dict 的情况，但实际 content 可能为 list，导致 SQLite INSERT 报错，数据无法持久化。
signals.review_reason: EventStore 是会话持久化的核心组件，content 类型处理不完整导致 SQLite 写入必现失败，所有包含 list 类型 content 的 run events 均无法存储，数据丢失，属于关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: [Bug] event_store存储content仅处理了dict的情况，但content存在为list的情况导致存储失败
source_issues.evidence: SQLite ProgrammingError: Error binding parameter 6: type 'list' is not supported。run结束后调用batch存储时触发，content 为 list 类型但代码只处理了 dict，导致 INSERT 失败，事件数据丢失。

signals.topic: Cline SDK migration causes staging authentication and task execution failures
signals.summary: Multiple users are blocked from logging in or executing tasks in the staging environment after the Cline SDK migration. Issues include unauthorized errors after login, infinite loading after canceling login, missing account tab details (name, email, environment), and missing browser settings options.
aliases: staging login fails after SDK migration
signals.review_reason: Five separate issues all trace back to the Cline SDK migration breaking staging authentication and settings. Users cannot log in, execute tasks, view account details, or configure browser settings in staging. This is a main-flow blocker for the staging environment and affects QA workflows.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Unauthorized error shown after login when executing tasks in Cline in staging environment
source_issues.evidence: User logs in via 'Sign up with Cline' in staging, then gets 'Unauthorized' error on every task execution. Video evidence provided.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Infinite loading shown on 'Sign Up With Cline' button after cancelling login process
source_issues.evidence: After canceling the login process mid-way, the 'Sign up with Cline' button shows infinite loading and is no longer clickable.

source_issues.title: [Cline SDK migration] Cline: Unable to login to staging environment
source_issues.evidence: User cannot log in to the staging environment after SDK migration. Video evidence provided.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Account tab details missing after upgrading to latest build (Name, Email, Environment option not displayed)
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading to latest build, the Account tab does not display user name, email, or environment option.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Browser settings option not visible in Cline Settings.
source_issues.evidence: Browser settings are not visible in the Settings panel after SDK migration. Video evidence provided.

aliases: vertex ai api key auth failure
signals.review_reason: Multiple non-Anthropic provider integrations are broken or unreliable. Vertex AI (GCP enterprise users) is completely blocked. DeepSeek plan mode and GPT 5.5 users experience intermittent or random failures. These represent significant user segments using non-default providers.

source_issues.title: Inconsistent web search-related error
source_issues.evidence: Web search raises an error in a half-full session but works after starting a new session. Reproduced with DeepSeek-v4 Pro model.

source_issues.title: Cline tool call error in plan mode
source_issues.evidence: All tool calls fail in a fresh session with DeepSeek-v4 Pro model in plan mode. Error occurs immediately on first tool call.

source_issues.title: Cline tool call error when using GPT5.5 - Cline stops in middle and advising me to use Sonnet 4.5
source_issues.evidence: Cline randomly stops mid-task when using GPT 5.5 and displays an error suggesting the user switch to Sonnet 4.5. Task is interrupted.

source_issues.title: [Bug] 'API keys are not supported by this API' when using Vertex AI in Kanban Agent Mode (Antigravity IDE / GCP VM)
source_issues.evidence: Using Vertex AI in a GCP corporate environment fails with 'API keys are not supported by this API'. Extension sends API key auth instead of OAuth2/ADC. GCP Project ID and Region fields also fail to persist in the UI.

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock: deprecated `temperature` parameter blocks Claude Opus 4.7
signals.summary: Claude Opus 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock returns an error because Cline sends a deprecated `temperature` parameter. Users cannot use Opus 4.7 via Bedrock at all.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users cannot use Claude Opus 4.7 via Amazon Bedrock due to Cline sending a deprecated temperature parameter. The model is completely inaccessible, blocking Bedrock users from using this specific model.

source_issues.title: Error using Claude Opus 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock: `temperature` is deprecated
source_issues.evidence: API request fails with: 'The model returned the following errors: temperature is deprecated for this model.' User cannot use Claude Opus 4.7 on Bedrock.

source_issues.title: Error using Claude Opus 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock: `temperature` is deprecated
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report. Same error message: temperature parameter deprecated for Opus 4.7 on Bedrock.

signals.topic: File write tool silently fails to persist changes to disk despite reporting success
signals.summary: replace_in_file tool reports 'The content was successfully saved' but the file on disk is never actually modified. User is billed for API calls without any actual changes being made, and must fall back to write_to_file (full overwrite) as a workaround.
aliases: replace_in_file reports success but file unchanged
signals.review_reason: This is a core workflow blocker: the replace_in_file tool lies about success, the user pays for API calls that produce no visible result, and they must manually fall back to write_to_file as a workaround. Any user relying on incremental edits will be unaware their changes were never saved.

source_issues.title: replace_in_file が反映されず、書き込まれなかったです。
source_issues.evidence: replace_in_file reports 'The content was successfully saved' but read_file and editor confirm file is unchanged. Reproduced across multiple Unity C# files. Workaround is write_to_file (full overwrite). User is billed for API usage with no actual output.

signals.topic: Terminal output reading freezes indefinitely on second command execution
signals.summary: Cline freezes on the second terminal interaction, showing 'Pending' status and never reading terminal output even after the command completes and the shell prompt returns.
aliases: terminal output not read after first command
signals.review_reason: This completely blocks any multi-step terminal workflow. The first command works but every subsequent command hangs indefinitely. The user cannot complete any task requiring more than one shell command, which is the majority of development tasks.

source_issues.title: Terminal interaction freezes on second interaction — Cline doesn't read terminal output after command completes
source_issues.evidence: After first terminal command succeeds, second command produces output and shell prompt returns but Cline shows 'Pending' and never reads the output. User provides exact reproduction command that triggers the freeze deterministically.

signals.topic: R2 subscription button in Cloudflare Dashboard non-functional — clicking 'Add R2 subscription to my account' only reloads page without completing subscription
signals.summary: 用户尝试通过 Dashboard 添加 R2 订阅时，点击订阅按钮后页面仅重新加载，未完成订阅操作，导致 R2 功能不可用、主流程被阻断。
aliases: Add R2 subscription button not working
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 有明确用户影响证据：点击订阅按钮后页面仅重载，R2 功能无法正常使用，主流程被阻断。非纯功能请求，属于真实用户痛点。因 count=1（单仓单条），不满足 P0 条件，标记为 P2。

source_issues.title: Please enable R2 through the Cloudflare Dashboard.
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告已启用 R2，点击 'Add R2 subscription to my account' 按钮后页面仅重新加载，未执行任何操作，附件截图显示按钮无响应。该问题阻断用户完成 R2 订阅配置，属于主流程失败。

signals.topic: Autocomplete code suggestions not working or showing incorrect content
signals.summary: The Continue autocomplete feature fails to provide code completions, or shows thinking/reasoning text instead of code suggestions. Users experience either no suggestions appearing, or suggestions polluted with internal model reasoning tokens that should be excluded.
signals.review_reason: Autocomplete is a primary differentiating feature of Continue. Its failure directly blocks the core coding-assistance workflow. Count=3 across three distinct but related root causes (UI not showing, reasoning tokens leaking, server response not registering). Multiple affected repos confirmed (vscode, openrouter provider). High user impact — code suggestions are the main deliverable of the product.

source_issues.title: Autocomplete for code is not working
source_issues.evidence: User reports autocomplete does nothing — no code suggestions appear at all. Tried disabling Copilot, small models, multiple configurations — all fail. YouTube video demonstrates the issue.

source_issues.title: Autocomplete using Openrouter doesn't send extraBodyProperties
source_issues.evidence: extraBodyProperties (reasoning exclusion settings) are not forwarded in OpenRouter autocomplete requests, causing thinking/reasoning tokens to appear in code suggestions instead of clean completions.

source_issues.title: Autocomplete does not register responses from server
source_issues.evidence: When using a non-standard API via proxy, autocomplete silently fails to display responses — UI shows 'incomplete' spinner indefinitely. User-provided screenshot confirms the registration failure. 6 comments, triaged and closed after investigation.

signals.topic: edit_existing_file silently fails without error feedback in VS Code
signals.summary: When using the edit_existing_file tool in VS Code, changes are sometimes not applied to the file even though the chat interface reports success. No error is shown, leading to AI-file state desync.
signals.review_reason: Two related but distinct file editing failures: (1) edit_existing_file silently no-ops with false success feedback, and (2) follow-up during edit suggestion causes state desync. Both directly break the core edit workflow and cause AI to produce incorrect subsequent output based on wrong file state. count=2 with confirmed user impact — files are not modified despite user intent and tool confirmation.

source_issues.title: edit_existing_file fails silently in VS Code integration, despite chat confirming success
source_issues.evidence: User clearly describes file content remaining unchanged after edit_existing_file, with chat falsely claiming 'File edited successfully.' No error message shown. Root cause hypothesized as VS Code file locking or race conditions. Affects all file types.

source_issues.title: Responding with a follow-up when AI suggests an edit results in desync
source_issues.evidence: When a follow-up is typed instead of accepting an AI edit suggestion, the edit is not carried out but the AI receives a success indicator — causing AI's file view to diverge from actual file state, leading to subsequent diff failures.

signals.topic: Continue extension inaccessible to screen reader users (NVDA, Orca)
signals.summary: The Continue VS Code extension is completely unusable with screen readers. Chat message history, action buttons, sidebar, and settings panel all lack accessibility labels, ARIA attributes, and keyboard navigation support.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct blind users explicitly report the extension is completely unusable with their respective screen readers (NVDA on Windows, Orca on Linux). This is a critical accessibility blocker — the product cannot be used at all by visually impaired developers. count=2 with explicit user testimony. P0 despite count=2 because the impact is absolute (complete feature denial for a user class) and the affected area spans the entire extension UI.

source_issues.title: Continue extension is completely inaccessible with NVDA screen reader — unlabeled buttons and inaccessible settings
source_issues.evidence: Blind user explicitly reports extension is 'completely unusable.' Action buttons (Insert, Copy, Apply, etc.) have no aria-label — NVDA reads them as 'unlabeled button.' Settings panel lacks keyboard navigation, form labels, and ARIA landmarks.

source_issues.title: A11Y: Continue sidebar doesn't work with screen readers in VS code
source_issues.evidence: Blind user (Orca screen reader on Ubuntu) reports being unable to use the chat interface at all. No labels on UI elements, cannot read chat history, VS Code accessibility settings not respected. 5 comments indicating community engagement.

signals.topic: IntelliJ/JetBrains plugin hijacks End key input
signals.summary: The Continue IntelliJ/JetBrains plugin intercepts End key presses even when no autocomplete suggestion is active, causing the cursor not to move to end-of-line on first press. Affects .toml files and other file types.
signals.review_reason: Two reports of identical End key behavior in IntelliJ/JetBrains IDEs with video evidence and YouTrack reference. While count=2, this is a high-quality UX regression that disrupts normal text editing every time a user presses End. JetBrains is a primary IDE for Continue. P1 due to frequency of occurrence but clear user impact on basic editing.

source_issues.title: Interferes with `End` key pressing
source_issues.evidence: Linked to YouTrack issue with video evidence. End key requires two presses to move cursor to end of line. First press triggers no movement (a small gap re-renders instead). Reported on IntelliJ.

source_issues.title: IntelliJ plugin hijacks End key
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 + IntelliJ 2026.1.1 + Continue 1.0.67. End key hijacked even with no autocomplete suggestion present (blank suggestion). YouTrack ticket with full reproduction steps. Cursor does not move on first press.

signals.topic: Continue Hub login fails with 401 'Not authenticated (user missing)'
signals.summary: Users who create a new Continue Hub account cannot log in — all login attempts result in a 401 Unauthorized error with message 'Not authenticated (user missing)'.
signals.review_reason: Login blocking is a clear auth issue that prevents users from accessing the Continue Hub service entirely. While count=1, the impact is absolute (account unusable from creation) and affects the paid/premium service tier. Classified as P1 rather than P0 due to single report, but genuine user-facing auth failure.

source_issues.title: Login failed with 'Not authenticated (user missing)' 401 error
source_issues.evidence: User creates a new Hub account but cannot log in at hub.continue.dev. All login attempts return 401 with 'Not authenticated (user missing)'. Support email addresses are also unreachable. Blocks entire Hub feature set.

signals.topic: HITL pre-review silently fails open, bypassing automated safeguards
signals.summary: When @human_feedback(learn=True) is used and lessons are recalled, any exception in _pre_review_with_lessons (network, auth, LLM error, structured-output issues) is caught and the original method_output is returned silently. No exception propagates, no warning is logged, callers cannot distinguish pre-reviewed output from raw model output — automated safeguards are silently bypassed.
signals.review_reason: This is a reproducible bug in a security-critical code path (human-in-the-loop). When the pre-review step fails, the system silently falls back to raw LLM output with no warning or exception, meaning automated safeguards provided by @human_feedback(learn=True) are bypassed without any user signal. Users cannot detect or act on this failure. The bug is in the production hot path and has a clear reproduction recipe.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: HITL pre-review fails open and silently bypasses automated safeguards
source_issues.evidence: Any exception in _pre_review_with_lessons is caught and original method_output returned silently. No exception propagates, no warning logged. Reproducible by patching the pre-review LLM call to raise RuntimeError — output is raw model output with no signal that pre-review failed. Downstream components cannot distinguish pre-reviewed from raw output.

signals.topic: BrightData SERP tool uses JS template literal syntax (${query}) in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
signals.summary: BrightDataSearchTool's get_search_url method uses ${query} (JavaScript template literal syntax) instead of {query} (Python f-string syntax), causing every search query to be prepended with a literal '$' character. All three engines (Google, Bing, Yandex) are affected, making all SERP searches return empty/wrong results.
aliases: SERP tool search query prefix dollar sign
signals.review_reason: A confirmed code defect in the BrightDataSearchTool that breaks all search queries in production. Every query is malformed, returning empty or wrong results. The bug affects a core tool integration (SERP searches) and has a clear reproduction path with evidence. Users cannot use the BrightData search tool at all until this is fixed.

source_issues.title: [BUG] BrightData SERP tool uses JavaScript template syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed code defect in brightdata_serp.py lines 132-137: f-string uses ${query} which Python interprets as literal '$' followed by interpolation. Search for 'AI news' produces 'https://www.google.com/search?q=$AI%20news' instead of '?q=AI%20news'. Affects all three search engines. Proof in Python shell included in report.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock Converse API native tool calls drop all arguments, always pass empty dict, causing pydantic validation failures on all tools with required parameters
signals.summary: When using AWS Bedrock as the LLM provider with native function calling, _parse_native_tool_call drops all tool arguments because Bedrock returns {name, input, toolUseId} without a 'function' key, causing func_info to be {} and func_args to default to '{}'. Every tool call receives an empty dict, triggering pydantic 'Field required' errors on any tool with mandatory parameters.
aliases: Bedrock Converse API empty dict tool calls
signals.review_reason: A confirmed bug in the Bedrock Converse API integration path that breaks ALL tool calls with required parameters. The bug is in a production code path, has a precise root cause identified, and causes pydantic validation failures that repeat until max iterations — completely blocking any crew using Bedrock with tools that have required arguments.

source_issues.title: [BUG] _parse_native_tool_call drops Bedrock Converse API tool arguments — always passes empty dict
source_issues.evidence: Exact bug location identified in crewai/agents/crew_agent_executor.py method _parse_native_tool_call: Bedrock returns {name, input, toolUseId} without a 'function' key. The dict handling branch sets func_info={}, func_args='{}', and the 'or' short-circuit prevents tool_call['input'] from being read. Reproducible error message: 'Field required [type=missing, input_value={}, input_type=dict]' repeating every iteration until max iterations. All tools with required parameters fail.

signals.topic: crewai create template ships Calculator tool using eval() on LLM-provided input, enabling remote code execution via indirect prompt injection
signals.summary: The AGENTS.md template bundled with crewai create includes a Calculator tool that calls eval(expression) on LLM-provided input. Every new project scaffolded with crewai create inherits this vulnerable pattern. Through indirect prompt injection (e.g., malicious document or website the agent processes), an attacker can achieve arbitrary code execution on the host, enabling data exfiltration and system compromise.
signals.review_reason: While there is no confirmed public victim, this is NOT a generic 'Security vulnerabilities' label — it is a specific, auto-propagating template vulnerability. The crewai create command automatically copies this vulnerable Calculator tool into EVERY new project, meaning all new users are exposed by default. The attack chain (indirect prompt injection -> eval() RCE) is practical and well-documented. This causes severe cost/data loss risk and is a clear user-facing security defect shipped in the default scaffold.

source_issues.title: [Security] crewai create ships template with eval() on unsanitized LLM input
source_issues.evidence: Affected file: lib/crewai/src/crewai/cli/templates/AGENTS.md line 773. The Calculator tool in the generated template calls eval(expression) directly on LLM output. Attack chain: malicious document -> LLM calls calculator tool -> arbitrary Python code executes. Impact documented: data exfiltration, full system compromise. This is NOT theoretical — the template is automatically copied into every new project via 'crewai create', meaning ALL new users are exposed.

signals.topic: Two parallel agent executor implementations (CrewAgentExecutor vs experimental AgentExecutor) cause architectural confusion and potential behavioral inconsistency
signals.summary: The repository maintains two parallel agent executor implementations (CrewAgentExecutor and experimental AgentExecutor) that both wire into the production hot path with no clear winner. Despite the 'experimental/' namespace, AgentExecutor is imported eagerly and instantiated unconditionally in Agent.kickoff(), while Agent.execute_task() still uses CrewAgentExecutor. This creates confusion about which executor runs, potential behavioral differences, and maintenance burden.
signals.review_reason: This is an architectural defect that creates confusion about executor behavior and which implementation is actually running in production. While not an immediate crash, it causes maintenance burden, potential behavioral inconsistency between the two paths, and difficulty for users debugging execution behavior. The misleading 'experimental/' namespace for production code is a UX issue that affects developers building on top of crewAI.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Two parallel agent executors (CrewAgentExecutor vs experimental AgentExecutor) cover the same responsibility — pick a winner
source_issues.evidence: Two parallel implementations both registered in _EXECUTOR_TYPE_REGISTRY and both wired into production hot path. AgentExecutor imported eagerly in crewai/__init__.py:75, instantiated unconditionally in Agent.kickoff() at agent/core.py:1402. But Agent.execute_task() at agent/core.py:1038 still calls self.executor_class which defaults to CrewAgentExecutor. No clear specification of which path is canonical. The 'experimental/' namespace is misleading.

signals.topic: API 调用因 temperature 参数已被模型废弃而返回 400 错误，导致主流程完全阻断
signals.summary: Opus-4.7 模型已废弃 temperature 参数，fabric 发送该参数后 API 返回 400 Bad Request，主流程失败。
signals.review_reason: API 请求因废弃参数直接返回 400，主流程完全失败。虽仅单条报告，但 API 废弃参数导致的阻断属于 P0 级别用户影响，不依赖频率判断。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Opus-4.7 temperature deprecated for this model
source_issues.evidence: API 返回 400 Bad Request: 'temperature is deprecated for this model'，fabric-ai v1.4.451 在 macOS Silicon 上通过 Homebrew 安装后，所有调用 Opus-4.7 的请求均失败，用户主流程完全阻断。

signals.topic: 未指定 -p 时 CLI 误将二进制名作为 pattern 使用，输出误导性错误信息并阻断常见入口操作
signals.summary: 调用 fabric-ai 不带 -p 参数时（如 `fabric-ai update` 或 `fabric-ai -y URL --transcript`），程序将 os.Args[0] 当作 pattern 名称查找，导致 'pattern fabric-ai not found' 误导错误，README 中的 zsh yt() 示例也因此失效，用户被引导往错误方向排查。
signals.review_reason: 未指定 -p 时程序崩溃式报错而非给出有用引导，且影响多个常见入口操作（transcript 提取、类 subcommand 调用），README 示例同时失效，用户体验显著下降。虽仅单条报告，但影响路径明确，属于可复现的阻断性问题。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Misleading "pattern '<binary-name>' not found" when no pattern is specified, plus README zsh yt() example is broken since #1960
source_issues.evidence: issue 明确提供可复现步骤，`fabric-ai update` 和 `fabric-ai -y URL --transcript` 均触发同一错误；README 中 zsh yt() 示例也因此失效（自 #1960 引入）；错误信息将二进制名误报为 pattern name，用户容易误判为未安装或 Homebrew 问题，review 中明确说明属于 bug 而非功能限制。

signals.topic: Repeated API 400 errors due to missing thought_signature on function calls
signals.summary: Function calls (run_shell_command, default_api:update_topic, etc.) are submitted without the required thought_signature field, causing the Gemini API to return 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT errors. This manifests across multiple issue reports as repeated request failures that block task completion.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: 3 distinct issue reports all trace back to the same root cause — function calls missing the required thought_signature field, causing API 400 errors that repeatedly fail requests and prevent tasks from completing. User explicitly reports 'this has been happening all day'. Clear user impact across multiple users.

source_issues.title: "Unable to submit request because function call `run_shell_command` in the 99. content block is missing a `thought_signature`"
source_issues.evidence: API Error 400: Unable to submit request because function call `run_shell_command` in the 99. content block is missing a `thought_signature`. Request failed completely. Windows, v0.41.2.

source_issues.title: Repeated API 400 error
source_issues.evidence: API 400 error: Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts. Position 20. API key auth. User reports 'this has been happening all day'.

source_issues.title: Repeated task processing
source_issues.evidence: Model keeps processing tasks repeatedly without stopping. User had to manually abort with ESC. Windows, v0.41.2. Related to the same thought_signature API error pattern.

signals.topic: Quota/billing display incorrectly reports 100% usage despite low or no actual CLI usage
signals.summary: On paid Google One AI Pro and Code Assist plans, the CLI status bar shows 'Quota Limit Reached' or '100% quota used' even when the user has made very few requests (3-4 prompts) or has not used the CLI at all. This leads to users being unable to use the service they are paying for.
aliases: quota limit reached without using CLI
signals.review_reason: Direct cost/availability impact: Paying users are blocked from using a service they are actively paying for due to incorrect quota tracking. Two independent reports confirm the same behavior. This is a revenue-affecting issue — users cannot access paid functionality despite having active subscriptions and sufficient quota.

source_issues.title: Limit Reached despite not using CLI
source_issues.evidence: User on Gemini Code Assist Pro plan reports 'Quota Limit is reached' displayed despite not using CLI for the day or only using it for 3-4 short prompts. Azure VM Linux user.

source_issues.title: Showing 100% quota reached on Google One Pro plan despite low usage
source_issues.evidence: User reports CLI status line shows 100% quota reached but session stats show only 27 total requests (14 Pro, 13 Flash) — far below daily limit for Google One AI Pro. Local UI misinterprets backend 429 errors or tool-call volume as total quota depletion. Also reports extreme 'Thinking' latency of 10+ minutes.

signals.topic: Corrupted oauth_creds.json causes Agent mode infinite crash loop (Windows)
signals.summary: On Windows, when oauth_creds.json is corrupted or has an invalid_grant token, the auth flow falls back to hitting the GCP metadata server (169.254.169.254), which always fails on local Windows machines. This causes the Agent background process to crash and restart infinitely, completely breaking Agent mode with no graceful recovery or re-auth prompt.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: Agent mode is entirely broken with an infinite crash loop. No graceful degradation or re-auth prompt is shown. Requires manual file deletion to fix. User is blocked from using the core Agent feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Agent mode stuck in infinite crash loop due to corrupted oauth_creds.json (Windows)
source_issues.evidence: Agent mode becomes completely unusable; background process crashes and restarts infinitely; workaround requires manually deleting oauth_creds.json to restore functionality

signals.topic: CLI deletes unintended files (over-deletes beyond user-specified scope, causing data loss)
signals.summary: The Agent mode CLI executed a delete operation that removed far more files than the user specified or intended — in one case deleting all personal files, photos, and game files when the user only asked to delete a specific folder. The delete command was scoped to one item but the CLI over-reached and destroyed unrelated user data.
signals.review_reason: Critical data destruction: The CLI's delete operation exceeded the user-specified scope and deleted all personal user data. This is a severe, direct data loss event — one of the most impactful failure modes possible. The user explicitly reported loss of important personal data and projects.

source_issues.title: cli gemini deleting file
source_issues.evidence: User reported CLI deleted all personal files, photos, and games instead of only the specific file/folder requested. Loss of important personal data and projects. Version 0.41.2, Windows, no sandbox.

signals.topic: CLI crashes on Alpine Linux due to unhandled PTY resize exception and musl IPC failure
signals.summary: Gemini CLI v0.42.0-nightly crashes immediately on Alpine Linux (musl libc) when attempting to execute shell commands. Two root causes: (1) the uncaughtException handler for PTY resize race conditions is guarded by process.platform === 'win32', so the same race on Alpine crashes the process; (2) the child-process relaunch mechanism using {ipc: true} silently fails on musl-based systems.
signals.review_reason: Platform blocking: Alpine Linux is a popular minimal container environment (Docker, serverless). The CLI crashes immediately on any shell command execution on this platform. This prevents a significant developer segment from using the CLI at all. Root cause is clearly identified and reproducible.

source_issues.title: bug: Gemini CLI crashes on Alpine Linux (musl libc) due to PTY resize error and relaunch IPC failure
source_issues.evidence: Gemini CLI crashes on Alpine Linux when executing shell tools/commands. Process exits immediately. Root cause identified in packages/cli/index.ts: PTY resize race uncaught exception not suppressed on non-Windows, and IPC channel fails on musl. Reproduction: docker run --rm -it node:alpine, npm install -g @google/gemini-cli@nightly, then run gemini with any shell command.

signals.topic: Codex integration broken — ignores 'never stop' instruction, blocking interactive sessions
signals.summary: Codex does not respect the 'never stop' instruction in autoresearch, causing interactive sessions to fail. This blocks users who prefer Codex over Claude from using the interactive session feature.
signals.review_reason: Direct user report with explicit blocking evidence: author states Codex 'doesn't work with autoresearch' due to ignoring 'never stop' instruction, which prevents interactive sessions — a key workflow the user depends on. User impact is clearly stated, not inferred.

signals.topic: SkillsMiddleware skips loading skills on first turn due to empty list guard bug
signals.summary: PrivateStateAttr initializes skills_metadata to [] by default, and SkillsMiddleware checks key existence rather than value emptiness. On the first agent turn, the guard skips skill loading, causing '(No skills available yet)' to appear in system prompts even when valid skills exist.
aliases: skills not loading on first invocation
signals.review_reason: Count >= 3 from independent reporters confirms this is a real, reproducible bug. The first turn of user interaction is blocked — skills are a core feature of the agent, and users consistently see '(No skills available yet)' even when skills are configured. This is a main-flow blocking issue for the initial agent interaction.

source_issues.title: SkillsMiddleware skips loading skills on first turn when skills_metadata=[] (PrivateStateAttr default)
source_issues.evidence: PrivateStateAttr initializes skills_metadata to [] by default. SkillsMiddleware.before_agent checks 'if skills_metadata in state: return None', but since the key always exists (with value []), the guard always returns early on the first turn. Three independent reports confirm this blocks the first-turn user experience.

signals.topic: Modal sandbox deploy template missing app= parameter causes deployment failure
signals.summary: The bundler-generated deploy_graph.py calls modal.Sandbox.create() without the required app= argument in modern Modal SDK (>=1.x), raising InvalidError and crashing the agent on first middleware invocation.
signals.review_reason: Deployment is a critical workflow and this bug completely blocks it — the bundler-generated deploy code crashes on first invocation. While count=2 (below the count>=3 threshold), review_reason provides explicit evidence of main-flow blocking: deployment is the primary user workflow and the generated code cannot run at all.

signals.topic: read_file tool description examples use wrong kwarg name (path vs file_path), causing validation errors and wasted turns
signals.summary: READ_FILE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION examples show path= but the schema declares file_path. Models follow the description literally, triggering Pydantic validation errors and wasting an LLM turn on every file read operation.
aliases: wrong kwarg in tool description examples
signals.review_reason: Two independent reporters confirm consistent per-file-read experience degradation: every file read wastes an LLM turn. This is not blocking but creates systematic overhead for any agent using filesystem operations. The bug is reproducible across multiple major versions.

source_issues.title: FilesystemMiddleware: read_file description shows examples with wrong kwarg name (path vs schema's file_path)
source_issues.evidence: Tool description examples use path= but the schema requires file_path. Every file read operation by the agent triggers Pydantic validation failure, causing the agent to waste a turn retrying. Reproducible across versions 0.4.1 through 0.6.0a1.

signals.topic: execute tool reports status='success' on non-zero exit code, causing agents to spiral on failures
signals.summary: The execute tool hardcodes status='success' even when commands fail with non-zero exit codes. Agents cannot distinguish success from failure and waste massive amounts of tokens on retry spirals.
aliases: execute tool hardcodes success on failure
signals.review_reason: Single report but with compelling production evidence: 8.8M tokens and 638 LLM turns wasted in a single incident. Main flow is blocked because agents cannot detect command failures and retry indefinitely. Downgraded to P1 from P0 because count=1 and the incident appears tied to a specific failure scenario rather than affecting all users.

source_issues.title: execute tool hardcodes status='success' on non-zero exit code
source_issues.evidence: The execute tool always sets status='success' regardless of exit code. In production, a FileNotFoundError caused an agent to waste 638 LLM turns and 8.8M tokens because status='success' gave no signal to stop retrying. With status='error', the agent would have recognized the persistent failure.

signals.topic: CompositeBackend write/edit operations emit spurious DeprecationWarning on every call
signals.summary: dataclasses.replace defeats the Unset sentinel by forwarding files_update=None to __init__, triggering a DeprecationWarning on every write/edit operation through CompositeBackend.
aliases: spurious warnings on every file write
signals.review_reason: Count=1 and experience degradation (noisy warnings) rather than blocking. Downgraded to P2 because the impact is limited to noisy output rather than flow blocking or cost loss. The warning is self-induced by the library code rather than a user-triggerable error.

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend.write/edit emits self-induced files_update DeprecationWarning via dataclasses.replace
source_issues.evidence: Every write/edit call through CompositeBackend triggers a DeprecationWarning. This self-induced warning is shown to users on every operation, creating a noisy experience and potentially masking other legitimate warnings.

signals.topic: langchain-deepseek: reasoning_content not passed back in multi-turn agent calls causing 400 errors
signals.summary: When using langchain-deepseek (v1.0.1) with thinking-mode models (deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-r1), agent.invoke() fails on the 2nd LLM call with 400 error because reasoning_content from the previous response is not included in the subsequent API request payload. ChatDeepSeek._get_request_payload() calls BaseChatOpenAI._convert_message_to_dict() which drops reasoning_content from AIMessage.additional_kwargs.
signals.review_reason: 4 duplicate issues all describing the same bug: multi-turn DeepSeek agent calls fail with 400 error on the 2nd LLM call because reasoning_content is dropped when serializing AIMessage to API payload. This is a complete workflow blocker for users using DeepSeek thinking-mode models in agentic workflows.

signals.topic: create_agent with response_format binds empty tools array, breaking OpenAI-compatible providers (vLLM v0.20.0+)
signals.summary: When using create_agent() with response_format=MySchema but no user tools, LangChain binds an empty tools array to the model request via model.bind_tools([]). vLLM v0.20.0+ validates that tools must either have at least one item or be omitted entirely, causing ValueError and agent invoke failure.
signals.review_reason: Agent creation with response_format (structured output) is a core use case. When no tools are provided, LangChain incorrectly sends an empty tools array instead of omitting the field, breaking OpenAI-compatible providers that validate this (e.g., vLLM v0.20.0+). Causes agent invoke to fail, blocking the structured-output agent workflow.

source_issues.title: create_agent with ProviderStrategy binds empty tools list and breaks OpenAI-compatible providers
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: `tools` must not be an empty array. Either provide at least one tool or omit the field entirely. Affects vLLM v0.20.0+ consistently.

signals.topic: configurable field lost in ToolRuntime.config when using tool_interceptors after upgrading to langchain-core 1.2.16 (regression from 1.2.15)
signals.summary: Regression between langchain-core 1.2.15 and 1.2.16: the configurable dict passed in RunnableConfig becomes empty when accessed via ToolRuntime.config inside tool_interceptors. Breaks any agent that relies on configurable values (db_config_id, user_id, etc.) in interceptor logic.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression between 1.2.15 and 1.2.16. The configurable field (used for passing context like db_config_id, user_id) is silently lost inside tool_interceptors. Any user who upgraded to 1.2.16 and uses configurable + tool_interceptors will have broken interceptor logic without obvious error messages.

source_issues.title: configurable field lost in ToolRuntime.config when using tool_interceptors in langchain 1.2.16 (works in 1.2.15)
source_issues.evidence: Regression: works in langchain-core 1.2.15, broken in 1.2.16. Interceptor prints {} for configurable instead of the passed values (db_config_id, user_id).

signals.topic: LangGraph SQL agent tutorial code example has unreachable interrupt branch with stream_mode='values'
signals.summary: The SQL agent tutorial code at docs.langchain.com uses stream_mode='values' and checks 'if messages in step' before 'elif __interrupt__ in step'. Since messages is always present in the step dict (stream_mode=values returns full state), the interrupt branch is never reached, and users following the tutorial cannot see interrupt details.
signals.review_reason: The official LangGraph SQL agent tutorial code is misleading: users following it cannot see interrupt output because the branch ordering is wrong. This is a documented code example on docs.langchain.com that leads users to believe the interrupt handling works, when it silently does not. Primary impact is user confusion and failed expectations in a learning context.

source_issues.title: A bug in learn-langgraph-SQL-agent
source_issues.evidence: Tutorial code: when stream_mode='values', step dict always contains 'messages' key. The interrupt check 'elif __interrupt__ in step' is never reached. User cannot see interrupt details in the tutorial output.

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators use lexicographic instead of numeric comparison, silently returning wrong query results
signals.summary: When using PostgresStore with numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte), comparisons are performed as text (lexicographic) rather than numeric, causing incorrect results. For example, filter={"score": {"$gte": 10}} incorrectly includes items with score=9 because '9' >= '10' in text ordering. This affects any production use of PostgresStore with numeric range queries.
signals.review_reason: Silently wrong query results in production PostgresStore is a critical data integrity failure. Numeric range filters silently include incorrect records. While count=1, the severity is P0: wrong data in database queries can have severe downstream consequences, and the fix in SqliteStore proves this is a known pattern that was missed in PostgresStore.

source_issues.title: Bug: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) use lexicographic (text) comparison instead of numeric comparison
source_issues.evidence: filter={"score": {"$gte": 10}} returns items with score=2..9 incorrectly. '9' >= '10' is True in text ordering. Reproducer shows all four operators use value->>%s with str param. SqliteStore already handles this correctly with CAST(... AS REAL) but fix was not propagated to PostgresStore.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud, causing 2-3x redundant work and cost
signals.summary: On LangGraph Cloud, tool calls taking longer than ~3 minutes are silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original is still running. Both original and duplicate complete successfully, causing 2-3x redundant LLM calls and tool executions. This is caused by a hardcoded 120s BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT that triggers a sweep of 'stale' runs.
signals.review_reason: Silent re-execution of long-running tool calls causes direct financial loss (2-3x redundant LLM calls) and corrupts agent state with duplicate side effects. This is a main-flow blocking issue on LangGraph Cloud for any legitimate long-running operation. Multiple environment variable workarounds were tried and failed.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: Tool calls >3min get silently re-dispatched. Both original and duplicate complete successfully, 2-3x redundant work and cost. BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 hardcoded in config/__init__.py. Queue sweep runs every 240s and calls Runs.Sweep(). Duplicate runs have identical tool call arguments, no preceding model node, indicating checkpoint-based re-dispatch. BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS=900 and BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS=true had no effect.

signals.topic: ensure_config mutates shared base config metadata, causing cross-invocation data leakage
signals.summary: When using langchain's create_agent with a shared base config metadata dict, ensure_config assigns it by reference without copying. This causes thread_id and other configurable values to leak from one invocation into the base config's metadata, contaminating all subsequent invocations with data from previous runs.
aliases: shared metadata dict corruption across invocations
signals.review_reason: Cross-invocation metadata contamination is a session state corruption issue. Thread IDs and other per-invocation data silently leaking into a shared base config means subsequent agent invocations operate with corrupted state. This is a P0: data leaks across user sessions are fundamentally blocking for multi-tenant or multi-thread deployments.

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: After ensure_config call, original_config metadata dict is mutated: {'metadata': {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent'}} becomes {'metadata': {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent', 'thread_id': 'thread-1'}}. The metadata dict from langchain>=1.2.13 base config is shared across all invocations, so data from previous runs leaks into future calls. Triggered by langchain-ai/langchain#35810.

signals.topic: Checkpoint serialization produces 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead with no opt-out path
signals.summary: LangGraph's checkpointer (MemorySaver, SqliteSaver, PostgresSaver) uses full Pydantic metadata serialization via dumpd() on every checkpoint write, producing 85% storage overhead and 37.8% token overhead in LLM context. There is no way to plug in an alternative serializer. Additionally, corrupt agent payloads silently pass through serialization without validation.
signals.review_reason: 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead on every checkpoint write is a significant cost amplifier at scale. The annual cost projection ($372,600 savings opportunity) quantifies real financial impact. While count=1, the severity and widespread nature (affects all checkpointers: MemorySaver, SqliteSaver, PostgresSaver) warrant P1.

source_issues.title: LangGraph checkpoint serialization produces 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead with no opt-out path - reproducible with drop-in fix
source_issues.evidence: 16-turn ReAct agent (65 messages): checkpoint 21,850 bytes vs 3,217 bytes with compact serializer (85.3% overhead). LLM context: 5,764 tokens vs 3,587 tokens (37.8% overhead). Financial projection: $764,200/year native JSON vs $391,600/year with compression (48.8% savings potential). No mechanism exists to plug in alternative serializer at checkpointer, store, stream, or subgraph boundary. Corrupt payloads (orphaned tool results, missing fields) silently reach LLM without validation.

signals.topic: allowed_msgpack_modules in langgraph.json not honored, causing Pydantic model degradation to dict on resume
signals.summary: When JsonPlusSerializer is configured with allowed_msgpack_modules to register framework types, it inadvertently enables strict mode which degrades user-defined Pydantic models to plain dicts on checkpoint resume. This causes AttributeError when user code tries to access Pydantic model attributes after resume, as 'dict' object has no attribute.
aliases: Pydantic model dict degradation on resume
signals.review_reason: Pydantic model degradation to dict on checkpoint resume is a session state corruption that causes runtime AttributeError. This breaks graph resumption for any user with typed state after using allowed_msgpack_modules, and the error only manifests after an interrupt/resume cycle making it hard to debug.

source_issues.title: Honor allowed_msgpack_modules in langgraph.json
source_issues.evidence: Setting allowed_msgpack_modules flips JsonPlusSerializer into strict mode. On resume, UserModel is degraded to dict and raises AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'label'. This is a cross-framework integration issue (e.g. UiPath-Langchain) where framework integrators need to register first-party types without breaking user types.

signals.topic: Workflow internal file uploads fail with 'Upload file <uuid> not found' under FileAccessController scope
signals.summary: In v1.14.0, workflows that internally generate files via file_service.upload_file() always fail with 'Upload file <uuid> not found' when the FileAccessController scope is active. The root cause is that source_url is generated via get_signed_file_url before the UploadFile row is committed to DB, causing _assert_upload_file_access() to query an uncommitted row. This is a regression affecting all workflow-based file generation scenarios.
aliases: workflow file upload fails scoped FileAccessController
Upload file not found workflow runtime
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression in v1.14.0 with explicit root cause analysis. It blocks the critical path of workflow-based file generation with high repro frequency (6x in 6 hours). While count=1, the severity and the explicit mention of superseding another issue (#35764) indicate a systemic regression.

source_issues.title: [1.14.0 regression] file_service.upload_file fails with "Upload file <uuid> not found" when scoped FileAccessController is active
source_issues.evidence: 6 occurrences in 6 hours under normal usage. Blocks all workflow internal file generation. Root cause traced to DB commit ordering in upload_file(). Only affects scoped execution, not /v1/files/upload (no scope).

signals.topic: File validation fails on multi-turn memory replay when custom file types are configured
signals.summary: In Chatflow/Agent modes with memory enabled and allowed_file_types containing 'custom', Round 1 file uploads succeed but Round 2+ replay from conversation history fails with 'File validation for file: <name>.png'. The validation logic only bypasses for literal FileType.CUSTOM but not when the upload was coerced from a custom slot to its detected type (e.g., image). This completely blocks multi-turn conversations that use custom file type configurations.
aliases: chatflow file validation memory replay fails
memory replay file type validation error
signals.review_reason: This bug completely blocks multi-turn conversations in Chatflow/Agent modes when custom file types are used. The failure is deterministic (round 2 always fails) and affects core functionality. The issue includes a detailed root cause analysis and clear reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: Chatflow file validation fails on memory replay when allowed_file_types is [custom]
source_issues.evidence: Round 1 works, Round 2 fails with ValueError. Affects ADVANCED_CHAT, CHAT, AGENT_CHAT modes with memory enabled. Root cause in is_file_valid_with_config: CUSTOM bypass triggers on literal type but not on resolved type post-upload. Reproduction confirmed on main branch.

signals.topic: Multi-turn conversation history lost in API integration — only initial message preserved
signals.summary: When using the API integration method, only the first interaction is stored. All subsequent conversation turns are lost in history, even though the AI response is completed successfully. The native Dify chat interface does not exhibit this issue, isolating it to the API integration path.
aliases: API mode history only first message
signals.review_reason: This is a clear data persistence bug in the API integration path that breaks the core value proposition of conversational AI. All messages after the first are lost, which is a critical user impact even at count=1. The contrast with the working native interface confirms a real bug rather than a usage error.

source_issues.title: Multi-turn conversation history is being lost
source_issues.evidence: User reports all subsequent messages lost in history via API integration. Native Dify chat interface works correctly. Database state shows messages are not being persisted for multi-turn via API. Clear user impact: conversation continuity is broken.

signals.topic: External knowledge base retrieval settings (top_k / score_threshold) not applied on save and retrieval testing

Retrieval testing also sends hard-coded defaults (top_k: 4, score_threshold: 0.5) instead of user-configured values. Users cannot customize external knowledge base retrieval behavior.
aliases: external knowledge base retrieval settings not saved
top_k score_threshold not applied external KB
external knowledge base config broken v1.14.0
signals.review_reason: This bug prevents users from configuring external knowledge base retrieval parameters, making the feature effectively non-functional for external providers. The crash is a TypeError that silently prevents saving, and retrieval testing ignores user settings entirely. This is a clear feature blockage in v1.14.0.

source_issues.title: [Bug] External knowledge base retrieval settings (top_k / score_threshold) are not applied on save and retrieval testing
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reranking_provider_name') at showMultiModalTip useMemo. Save button click fires no PATCH request. Retrieval testing sends hard-coded top_k:4/score_threshold:0.5 instead of user-configured values. Confirmed on v1.14.0.

The workflow works normally in the preview interface but hangs and causes the entire conversation to disappear on the standalone page.

standalone run page hangs file input
