The hang causes the conversation to disappear, representing significant user experience damage. Though count=1, the impact (complete process block + conversation loss) warrants P1.

source_issues.title: File variables can cause the process to hang
source_issues.evidence: Process hangs with no output on standalone run page. Works in preview. Affects hidden optional file variables. Conversation disappears after hang. Deterministic reproduction described.

signals.topic: openclaw-mem0 plugin crashes on Windows with OpenClaw 5.4, blocking autoRecall/autoCapture
signals.summary: The @mem0/openclaw-mem0 v1.0.11 plugin fails to load on Windows when using OpenClaw 5.4 with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME. Both autoRecall and autoCapture features are completely unusable on Windows. Users must downgrade to OpenClaw 5.2 as workaround.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking on a supported platform (Windows). Both autoRecall and autoCapture are completely unusable — no memories are saved or retrieved. Workaround (downgrade) is non-trivial for enterprise users.

source_issues.title: [Bug] @mem0/openclaw-mem0 v1.0.11 fails on Windows with OpenClaw 5.4: ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME
source_issues.evidence: Plugin crashes with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME, making memory features completely unusable on Windows. Workaround requires downgrading OpenClaw to 5.2.

signals.topic: TypeScript SDK v3 silently camelizes user-defined metadata keys on read, breaking round-trip for existing applications
signals.summary: The v3 TypeScript SDK's snakeToCamelKeys utility recursively transforms all nested objects including user-controlled metadata blobs. Any snake_case key in metadata (e.g., message_id, supplier_id, database_name) is silently converted to camelCase on read, causing application code that filters by metadata fields to silently fail. This is a data corruption issue that breaks existing v2 code after upgrade with no warning.
signals.review_reason: Data corruption issue — metadata round-trip is silently lossy. Existing v2 SDK code upgrading to v3 breaks silently with no error, causing undefined behavior in application-level code reading metadata fields. Confidence high due to detailed repro and multi-app impact described.

source_issues.title: [TypeScript SDK] v3 silently camelizes user-defined metadata keys on read, breaking round-trip
source_issues.evidence: User reports: indexer silently classifies all new memories as invalid (metadata.databaseName now instead of database_name), keyword index fragmented by pre/post-upgrade keys, adapters returning undefined for newly written memories. Behavior change vs v2 with no error/warning.

signals.topic: Delete API returns success response but memory is not actually deleted (silent failure)
signals.summary: When calling the delete API (/product/delete_memory), the API returns a success response but the memory still appears in search results and its delete_time field remains empty, indicating no actual deletion occurred. This is a silent failure that corrupts the user's memory state.
aliases: memory not deleted despite success response
signals.review_reason: Silent failure on a core CRUD operation. The delete API gives no indication of failure while leaving stale data in the system, making memory management fundamentally unreliable. Actively discussed with 4 comments confirming the issue.

source_issues.title: delete api doesn't work
source_issues.evidence: Delete API returns success but memory still appears in search and delete_time field is empty. 4 comments indicate the issue is actively discussed and confirmed.

signals.topic: Server mode multimodal messages API rejects valid image_url content with validation error
signals.summary: In server mode, the /memories POST endpoint returns a Pydantic validation error when messages contain image_url content (multimodal), even though image_url is a valid content type in modern LLM pipelines. Users trying to add memories with image URLs get 'Input should be a valid string' validation error.
aliases: image_url content rejected by server API
signals.review_reason: Key multimodal use case blocked by a validation error. Users cannot add memories with image content in server mode, which is a valid and common AI agent pattern.

source_issues.title: I started in server mode and adding memories is not supported in multi-modal mode.
source_issues.evidence: POST /memories with image_url content returns 'Input should be a valid string' validation error. Multimodal use case (e.g., processing receipts) is blocked.

signals.topic: openclaw-mem0 plugin agent isolation and run_id broken after OpenClaw 4.26+ upgrade
signals.summary: After upgrading @mem0/openclaw-mem0 to v1.0.11 on OpenClaw 4.26+, agent-level memory isolation is broken (user_id not concatenated with agent suffix), run_id is always None preventing session filtering, and autoCapture saves no memories. Root cause is that OpenClaw 5.3+ calls register() multiple times per conversation, creating separate closures that don't share state.
signals.review_reason: Multiple core plugin features broken after an upgrade path: agent isolation, session filtering, and auto-save all fail. This breaks a core memory plugin for users who upgrade OpenClaw, with no fix in the official plugin yet (user created a patch fork).

source_issues.title: [openclaw-mem0] Agent isolation & run_id broken after OpenClaw 4.26+ upgrade
source_issues.evidence: Agent-level memory isolation broken (user_id not concatenated with :agent:<agent_id> suffix), run_id always None preventing session-level filtering, autoCapture broken (no memories saved). Root cause identified as register() called multiple times per conversation.

signals.topic: .NET v1.5.0 regression: Anthropic and Google GenAI packages completely broken due to Microsoft.Extensions.AI breaking changes
signals.summary: AnthropicClient and GoogleGenAIClient crash with MissingMethodException in v1.5.0 after upgrading from v1.4.0-preview, caused by breaking API changes in Microsoft.Extensions.AI WebSearchToolResultContent. OpenAI packages also affected.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression from v1.4.0 to v1.5.0 that causes a runtime crash (MissingMethodException), completely breaking Anthropic and Google GenAI provider integrations. All users upgrading to v1.5.0 who use these providers are blocked. Count=1 (single issue) limits to P1 despite severity, as P0 requires count>=3 per priority rules.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: In v. 1.5.0 Microsoft.Agents.AI.Anthropic (and Google.GenAI) do not work [Regression]
source_issues.evidence: MissingMethodException on WebSearchToolResultContent.Results property breaks all Anthropic and Google GenAI users after upgrading to v1.5.0 from v1.4.0-preview. Stack trace shows crash in PopulateResponseContents. Both providers confirmed affected.

signals.topic: .NET: OpenAI-compatible extra body 'thinking' field not forwarded to provider endpoints
signals.summary: Provider-specific body fields like 'thinking' for ARK/other OpenAI-compatible backends are silently dropped by Microsoft.Agents.AI.OpenAI, blocking extended thinking and reasoning features on non-OpenAI endpoints.
aliases: extended thinking not working on third-party backends
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional gap where provider-specific body fields are silently dropped, preventing extended thinking/thinking budgets from working on OpenAI-compatible third-party backends. Users are actively blocked from using key model capabilities. Count=1 limits to P1 despite blocking nature.

source_issues.title: .NET: OpenAI-compatible extra body field thinking is not forwarded when using Microsoft.Agents.AI.OpenAI
source_issues.evidence: Provider-specific 'thinking' field is present in AgentRunOptions.AdditionalProperties but is silently stripped before the outgoing HTTP request, confirmed by intercepting the JSON payload via local proxy. Users trying to use extended thinking on ARK endpoints (doubao-seed model) are blocked.

signals.topic: Python: YAML block scalar parsing silently truncates multi-line descriptions in file skill frontmatter
signals.summary: Python's _extract_frontmatter() uses a regex that only handles single-line key-value pairs, silently truncating YAML block scalars (|, >, |-, >+) to just the indicator character. Multi-line skill descriptions become literally '|' instead of the actual text.
signals.review_reason: This is a data corruption bug where multi-line skill descriptions are silently truncated, making file-based skills with multi-line descriptions unusable. This is confirmed by .NET counterpart fix (PR #5610 already merged), indicating the issue is well-understood. No workaround available for Python users.

source_issues.title: Python: Fix YAML block scalar parsing in file skill frontmatter
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code shows that YAML block scalar literal (|) used for multi-line descriptions is truncated to just the pipe character. Example: description becomes '|' instead of the full multi-line text. This silently corrupts skill metadata and is a port of an already-merged .NET fix (PR #5610).

signals.topic: Hosted agent Responses REST endpoint: missing or invalid api-version causes 404 errors, documentation is unclear
signals.summary: The hosted agent Responses endpoint requires api-version query parameter but returns 404 when the documented 2025-11-15-preview version is used, and returns 400 when omitted. Users cannot successfully call the endpoint.
aliases: Azure Foundry hosted agent REST API versioning broken
signals.review_reason: Users are blocked from calling the hosted agent Responses REST API due to api-version confusion. The documented version returns 404, and the endpoint fails without it. This is a complete workflow block for users trying to integrate via REST.

source_issues.title: Hosted agent Responses endpoint requires api-version
source_issues.evidence: Step-by-step reproduction: sending POST to the documented endpoint without api-version returns 400 BadRequest; retrying with the documented api-version=2025-11-15-preview returns 404. Users are completely blocked from using the hosted agent Responses REST API.

signals.topic: .NET Workflow Host-as-Agent message reordering in non-streaming mode with tool calls and handoffs
signals.summary: When using Workflow with tool calls and responses wrapped in .AsAgent(), the MessageMerger produces incorrect message ordering in RunAsync mode. This manifests in history with merged order but the underlying data is wrong.
aliases: tool call response ordering broken handoff workflows
signals.review_reason: This is a functional bug affecting workflow execution correctness when using non-streaming mode with tool calls and handoffs. The message ordering is silently wrong, leading to incorrect agent state. Count=1 limits to P1.

source_issues.title: .NET: Workflow Host-as-Agent can improperly reorder messages in history and when running non-streaming
source_issues.evidence: MessageMerger topology sort and merge produces unexpected message ordering in the presence of ToolCalls/Responses in Handoff workflows. Visible in RunAsync mode; hidden in RunStreamingAsync mode where raw event order is used. Results in incorrect agent history.

signals.topic: MagenticOne CLI crashes on startup with UnicodeDecodeError on non-English system encoding
signals.summary: playwright_controller.py opens a JavaScript file without specifying encoding='utf-8', causing UnicodeDecodeError (e.g. cp950 codec) on systems with non-English default encoding (Traditional Chinese, Japanese, etc.), completely blocking MagenticOne startup.
signals.review_reason: The UnicodeDecodeError is a real crash that blocks the entire MagenticOne CLI from starting on non-English systems (Windows cp950, Japanese cp932, etc.). The user could not run any agent task. While only 1 issue, the severity is high — complete workflow blockage on a documented feature (MagenticOne MultimodalWebSurfer) for any non-English speaking user.

source_issues.title: open needs encoding='utf-8' for non-english environment, error in playwright_controller.py
source_issues.evidence: Crash at playwright_controller.py line 68: UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp950' codec can't decode byte 0xe2 in position 11569. User ran m1 CLI with Chinese input and MagenticOne crashed immediately on startup before any agent task could run. The same codebase-wide issue of missing explicit encoding in open() calls also affects other files.

signals.topic: Protobuf cross-language message routing silently drops messages with 'Unhandled Message' / 'Unknown Payload' errors
signals.summary: Messages published from Python agents (NewMessageReceived, Output with proto_data) in the distributed runtime are silently dropped and logged as 'Unhandled Message: message:...' or 'UnknownPayload' errors, breaking cross-language (dotnet↔python) multi-agent communication.
signals.review_reason: Protobuf-based cross-language messages are silently dropped in the distributed runtime — the handler's @message_handler never receives NewMessageReceived or Output proto_data messages, producing repeated 'Unhandled Message' log entries. This breaks a core distributed multi-agent communication contract: messages are published but never delivered, completely blocking multi-agent workflows across dotnet/python boundaries.

source_issues.title: some messages published from python are routed to the agent but result in either Unhandled Message or Unknown Payload.
source_issues.evidence: Logs show NewMessageReceived and Output messages published from Python (cloudEvent with proto_data containing NewMessageReceived/value='from Python!') are received back from the host as 'Unhandled message: message: "from Python!"' and 'Unhandled message: UnknownPayload(type_name="", data_content_type="application/x-protobuf", payload=b"")'. The handler never receives these messages, breaking agent-to-agent communication in the distributed runtime.

signals.topic: AutoGen Studio WebSocket endpoint accepts unauthenticated team_config leading to RCE via exec(source_code)
signals.summary: AutoGen Studio WebSocket handler accepts attacker-controlled team_config without authentication by default (AuthConfig type='none'), directly passing user-supplied source_code to Python's exec(), enabling pre-auth RCE with CVSS 9.8.
aliases: AutoGen Studio RCE via FunctionTool source_code
signals.review_reason: This is a pre-authentication RCE vulnerability with a complete public PoC. Any AutoGen Studio deployment using default configuration is remotely exploitable — an unauthenticated attacker sends malicious Python code via WebSocket and achieves arbitrary code execution on the server. This is the most severe user-impacting security flaw: server compromise, credential theft, and complete system takeover with zero prerequisites.

source_issues.title: [Security] Critical: Unauthenticated RCE via WebSocket team_config (CVSS 9.8)
source_issues.evidence: CVSS 9.8 Critical. Default AuthConfig sets type='none'. WebSocket handler accepts team_config without validation. FunctionTool._from_config() calls exec(source_code) directly with no sandbox. A fully public PoC is included: attacker sends malicious FunctionTool source_code via WS /api/ws/runs/{run_id} to achieve arbitrary code execution on the host server. No authentication or user interaction required.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing, enabling host compromise via prompt injection
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a subprocess without any filesystem isolation, network restrictions, or sandbox — only a UserWarning is emitted which is easily suppressed in production, leading to credential theft or system compromise via indirect prompt injection.
aliases: exec() of LLM-generated code without sandbox
signals.review_reason: This is a critical design flaw in a documented and quickstart-recommended code executor. When users follow official examples and use LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor, LLM-generated code runs with full host privileges and no sandbox. Indirect prompt injection attacks (malicious content in web pages, documents, user messages) can cause the LLM to generate credential-theft code that executes with the same privileges as the Python process. The UserWarning safeguard is trivially bypassed in any production deployment.

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: Code path writes LLM-generated code to disk (self.work_dir / filename) then executes via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with full host privileges. Only a UserWarning is emitted at __init__ time, which is silently swallowed in production configurations (-W ignore, logging pipelines). Attack scenario: attacker uses indirect prompt injection to make LLM generate malicious code (e.g. curl exfil of ~/.ssh/id_rsa), which is then written and executed with full host access.

signals.topic: Dashboard screencast permanently freezes on frame acknowledgment failures and does not recover
signals.summary: Dashboard video feed permanently freezes when frame acknowledgments fail (network timeout, connection issues), with no recovery mechanism. Uses sendMayFail() which silently swallows errors. Requires full dashboard restart to recover.
signals.review_reason: Dashboard screencast is a key debugging feature. Once it freezes, it never recovers and the entire dashboard must be restarted. This is significant UX degradation for remote browser debugging workflows. Two independent issues confirm the same problem pattern.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Dashboard screencast freezes on frame acknowledgment failures
source_issues.evidence: Dashboard video feed freezes permanently when frame acknowledgments fail (network timeout, connection issues). sendMayFail() silently swallows errors. No recovery mechanism - requires full restart.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Dashboard interactive clicks fail with remote browsers and screencast freezes
source_issues.evidence: Bug #2: Screencast freezes on frame acknowledgment failures. Makes the Dashboard's primary debugging visibility feature unusable.

signals.topic: HAR replay serves failed retry response due to duplicate HAR entries
signals.summary: routeFromHAR with update:true saves both failed (empty body) and successful responses for retried requests, causing HAR replay to serve the first broken entry and produce blank pages or stale content.
signals.review_reason: HAR replay core functionality is broken: tests relying on HAR network simulation silently serve corrupted/empty responses from failed retry attempts. This is not an edge case—it actively produces wrong test outcomes (blank pages, auth failures) that are hard to diagnose since HAR recording/replay is opaque.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: routeFromHAR records duplicate entries for retried requests, causing replay to serve failed response
source_issues.evidence: When routeFromHAR records with update:true and a request is retried after transient failure, both failed (empty body) and successful responses are saved as separate entries. HAR replay serves the first (broken) entry, causing blank pages and test failures. Real reproduction with flaky-server endpoint provided.

signals.topic: HAR recording truncates cookie values containing '=' due to incorrect parsing
signals.summary: Cookie headers with '=' in values (Base64 tokens, JWT cookies, URL-encoded values) are silently truncated at the first '=' during HAR recording, causing HAR replay to send corrupted authentication cookies.
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption in HAR recordings causes authentication failures on replay. Cookie values with '=' are common for Base64-encoded tokens, JWT cookies, and URL-safe encoded values. Users debugging HAR-based test replays will see wrong behavior with no indication that the HAR data itself was corrupted during recording.

source_issues.title: fix(har): API request cookie values containing '=' are truncated in HAR recording
source_issues.evidence: Cookie header 'token=abc=xyz; other=val' recorded in HAR as 'token=abc' due to split('=') bug instead of indexOf('=') in fetch.ts. Affects Base64 tokens, JWT cookies, URL-encoded values. HTTP request sent correctly; only HAR recording corrupted. Reproduction: value 'token=abc=xyz' becomes 'token=abc'.

signals.topic: Dashboard interactive mode sends clicks to wrong coordinates (0,0) for remote browsers
signals.summary: When using connectOverCDP(), Android, or iOS remote debugging, dashboard interactive clicks go to (0,0) instead of the intended coordinates, making the interactive debugging feature completely unusable for remote browser workflows.
signals.review_reason: The Dashboard's interactive mode is a key feature for remote browser debugging workflows (CDP, Android, iOS). When clicks land at (0,0) instead of the intended element, the entire interactive debugging workflow is broken. This blocks the primary use case of remote browser debugging through the Dashboard.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Dashboard interactive clicks fail with remote browsers and screencast freezes
source_issues.evidence: Dashboard interactive clicks go to (0,0) instead of intended coordinates when using connectOverCDP(), Android, or iOS remote debugging. Makes remote debugging via Dashboard completely unusable.

signals.topic: MCP extension mode rejects all browser-level CDP commands (Storage, Browser) with 'Unsupported command without sessionId'
signals.summary: In MCP extension mode, all browser-level CDP commands (Storage.*, Browser.*) fail with 'Unsupported command without sessionId', breaking cookie-list, cookie-get, cookie-set, state-save. Root cause in cdpRelayV2.ts unconditionally requires sessionId for all commands.
signals.review_reason: Extension mode's primary use case—reading HttpOnly cookies from a user's logged-in browser—is completely broken. This blocks the core workflow for the MCP/extension integration, not a peripheral feature. Root cause is a single conditional in cdpRelayV2.ts.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: cli-client extension mode rejects all browser-level CDP commands (cookie-list, state-save) with 'Unsupported command without sessionId'
source_issues.evidence: In MCP extension mode, Storage.* and Browser.* CDP commands fail with 'Unsupported command without sessionId'. Breaks cookie-list, cookie-get, cookie-set, state-save. Root cause: cdpRelayV2.ts unconditionally requires sessionId for all commands.

signals.topic: VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions not passed to EmbeddingGenerationOptions — blocks MRL embedding models
signals.summary: When using text embedding models with MRL (Matryoshka Representation Learning) support, users cannot enable automatic embedding generation because VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions cannot be passed to EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions through the automatic embedding generation flow.
signals.review_reason: This is a real functional gap: MRL-capable embedding models cannot leverage automatic embedding generation without manual workarounds. The issue prevents users from using reduced-dimension embeddings (a standard performance optimization for vector databases) in the SK automatic embedding pipeline. Not P0 because count=1 and the core embedding generation still works — only the dimension control is blocked.

source_issues.title: `VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions` should be passed to `EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions`
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'while we are using text embedding models with MRL support, we could not use automatic embedding generation. It is because we have no way to specify `EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions` via automatic embedding generation flow.' This is a clear feature gap causing inability to use MRL-capable embedding models in the automatic embedding pipeline.

signals.topic: ImageContent in kernel function results serialized as JSON instead of native image format — breaks multimodal tool results
signals.summary: When a kernel function returns ImageContent, FunctionCallsProcessor serializes it to JSON string. This prevents connectors (Gemini 3+, Anthropic Claude) that natively support images in tool results from receiving actual image objects, causing the model to receive base64 text instead of a viewable image.
aliases: ImageContent serialized as JSON in tool results
tool result image format not native
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug with clear user impact: multimodal connectors (Gemini 3+, Anthropic Claude) that natively support images in tool results receive broken JSON text instead of native image objects. The issue has a precise reproduction path and the bug is acknowledged (closed with fix). This blocks the use of ImageContent in function-calling scenarios — a core multimodal AI feature.

source_issues.title: Bug: ImageContent in tool/function results is serialized to JSON instead of native format
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with clear reproduction steps: kernel function returning ImageContent results in serialized JSON text in API requests instead of native image format (inlineData for Gemini 3+, ImageBlockParam for Anthropic). The model receives '{ "Data": "base64...", "MimeType": "image/png" }' as text instead of an actual image it can 'see'. Confirmed closed on 2026-05-07.

signals.topic: Codex Browser Use / in-app browser disappears mid-session and Chrome extension content APIs fail with nodeRepl.fetch errors
signals.summary: Two related browser plugin issues: (1) Browser Use in Codex Desktop disappears mid-session without user action, showing plugin unavailable. (2) Chrome extension can list and claim tabs but content-level APIs (text, DOM snapshot, screenshot) all fail with 'nodeRepl.fetch request failed'. The Chrome extension has full permissions and is connected, but page content APIs are non-functional. Also: domSnapshot on authenticated pages can crash the user's actual Chrome profile.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用: Browser Use 是 Codex Desktop 的核心差异化功能之一。三条 issue 分别描述该功能在会话中消失、内容 API 全部失败（nodeRepl.fetch）、甚至导致用户真实 Chrome 浏览器崩溃。这些不是边缘问题，而是核心插件功能反复失败。issue 21822 明确指出 extension 已正确授权但内容读取全部报错，属于系统性功能缺陷。

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop: Browser Use / in-app browser disappears mid-session without user reload
source_issues.evidence: Browser Use works normally then disappears mid-session without manual reload. User continues conversation and Browser Use disappears again. Settings then show the plugin as unavailable. Recurs without user action.

source_issues.title: Chrome extension can list/claim tabs but page content APIs fail with nodeRepl.fetch request failed
source_issues.evidence: Codex Chrome extension shows Connected with full site access but all content-level APIs (rendered text, headlines, DOM snapshot, visible DOM, screenshot) fail with 'nodeRepl.fetch request failed'. Tab listing and claiming works, but content reading is completely non-functional.

source_issues.title: Chrome plugin domSnapshot on authenticated Blackboard page crashed Google Chrome profile
source_issues.evidence: Using Codex Chrome plugin to call tab.playwright.domSnapshot() on an authenticated Blackboard page caused the user's real Google Chrome profile (not the Codex browser) to crash/exit. This is a crash of the user's actual browser, not an internal Codex component.

signals.topic: Codex Desktop conversation scroll jumps ~10+ pages upward after submit, scrollbar/End/PageDown unresponsive in long threads
signals.summary: After pressing Enter in a long thread, the conversation jumps up ~10 pages instead of staying at the newest response. All scroll navigation controls (End, Ctrl+End, Page Down, slider) are broken, requiring manual scrolling. Restarting does not fix it. Affects Codex Desktop on Windows in threads with many pasted code blocks, tool outputs, and images.
aliases: tmux window split causes message loss
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断: 在长对话线程中，提交消息后对话内容跳回10+页且所有滚动导航失效，用户无法阅读最新回复，必须手动滚屏。这不是边缘体验下降，而是直接阻断核心对话阅读流程。issue 21834 明确描述滚动控件全部失效且重启不修复，属于高严重性 bug。issue 21811 虽为单仓单例，但同属 scroll/消息可见性问题，合并为 count=2。

source_issues.title: Slider and window repositioning not working correctly
source_issues.evidence: In a long thread, after pressing Enter to send a message, the conversation jumps upward roughly 10 pages instead of staying at the newest response. The scrollbar, End, Ctrl+End, and Page Down all do not work. Restarting Codex does not fix it. The thread contains many long pasted code blocks, tool outputs, and images.

source_issues.title: Last message disappears when splitting tmux window
source_issues.evidence: When changing the size of the UI (e.g., zooming a pane in a tmux window), the last message from the AI disappears. /copy does not work over SSH, leaving no way to recover the message except re-requesting and burning tokens.

signals.topic: Codex VSCode extension corrupts git repositories with 'fatal: unable to read sha' and worktree index.lock race conditions on cold start
signals.summary: The Codex VSCode extension causes git repository corruption on VS Code cold start when using git worktrees. Bisected to the Codex extension. Causes 'fatal: unable to read sha' or 'Unable to create .git/worktrees/.../index.lock: File exists' errors. Affects Linux VS Code + Codex extension users with git worktrees. Users must run git reset --hard or delete index.lock to recover.
aliases: git index.lock race condition on cold start
fatal: unable to read sha bisected to Codex
signals.review_reason: 关键数据损坏: Codex VSCode 扩展在 VS Code 冷启动时与 git worktree index 产生竞争条件，导致仓库进入损坏状态（'fatal: unable to read sha'）。用户必须手动修复（git reset --hard 或删除 index.lock）。已明确 bisect 到 Codex 扩展本身，非外部因素。这是影响开发者核心工作流的严重 bug，且在生产环境（truffleruby 等大型仓库）中可稳定复现。

source_issues.title: Codex VSCode extension corrupts git repositories with `fatal: unable to read sha` and `fatal: Unable to create '.../.git/worktrees/foo/index.lock': File exists.`
source_issues.evidence: Bisected to Codex extension. Does not happen with Codex extension disabled. Happens more than half the tries with extension enabled. Workaround requires `git reset --hard HEAD` or deleting index.lock files. Users report needing to disable or uninstall Codex extension to prevent repository corruption.

signals.topic: Windows sandboxed Codex shell sessions cannot access Windows Credential Manager / keyring for gh auth, breaking GitHub workflows
signals.summary: On Windows, gh auth status fails in sandboxed Codex shell sessions with invalid token error, while the same command succeeds in full-access sessions. The sandboxed session cannot see GitHub CLI credentials stored in Windows Credential Manager (cmdkey /list shows no entries). This blocks all GitHub-dependent Codex workflows (git operations, gh CLI) on Windows in sandbox mode even when gh auth is valid outside the sandbox.
aliases: gh auth keyring inaccessible in sandbox
Windows Credential Manager not visible in sandboxed sessions
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断: Windows 沙箱环境下，Codex 无法访问 Windows Credential Manager 中存储的 gh auth 凭据，导致所有 GitHub 相关工作流（git 操作、gh CLI）全部失败。这是沙箱安全的核心功能缺失，直接阻断 Windows 用户在沙箱模式下的 GitHub 开发工作流。

source_issues.title: Windows sandboxed sessions cannot access valid gh keyring auth that works in full-access mode
source_issues.evidence: In sandboxed Codex shell sessions on Windows, gh auth status fails with 'The token in default is invalid.' while the same gh binary with the same auth succeeds in full-access sessions. cmdkey /list in sandboxed session shows no GitHub CLI credential targets. This is a sandbox/session integration issue with Windows Credential Manager or keyring visibility.

signals.topic: Detached background task-worker exits silently without writing failed status when broker socket disconnects, leaving ghost 'running' tasks
signals.summary: When a background task-worker process exits due to broker JSON-RPC socket close/reset, the catch block is never reached and no failed status is written. The job stays permanently in 'status: running' with a dead PID. Operators cannot distinguish dead tasks from live ones and must manually ps -p to check and mark tasks failed. Blocks automated job monitoring and reliable CI/CD pipeline integration.
aliases: Task status stuck in running after disconnect
Background task status not updated on worker exit
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断: 后台任务工作进程在 broker socket 断开时静默退出，任务状态永远停留在 'running'，operators 无法区分存活任务和死任务。这直接破坏后台任务监控体系的可靠性，影响 CI/CD 流水线集成。已提供具体代码位置和两次实际复现证据。

source_issues.title: Detached task-worker exits without writing failed status on broker socket disconnect
source_issues.evidence: When broker JSON-RPC socket closes/resets, task-worker process dies silently. runTrackedJob's catch block is never reached. The job stays permanently in status: 'running' with a dead PID. Two ghost-running tasks observed with last activity timestamps minutes before broker reset, then no log entries, no error, dead PIDs. Operators must ps -p to distinguish dead tasks from live ones.

signals.topic: OpenAIConversationsSession persistence returns 400 API errors

signals.review_reason: Session persistence completely broken for two distinct item types; both return 400 API errors and block any agent using OpenAIConversationsSession with reasoning or file_search features. Count=2 confirms this is a repeated pattern.

signals.summary: OpenAIChatCompletionsModel silently ignores reusable prompts (Responses API feature) and accepts previous_response_id/conversation_id without sending them to the provider, causing loss of server-managed conversation state.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct acceptance-but-no-op behaviors in Chat Completions model; both are silent failures that mislead callers into believing prompts or conversation state are active when they are not.

signals.topic: Sandbox path traversal via absolute paths bypasses base_dir
signals.summary: LocalFile, LocalDir, and GitRepo all accept absolute paths in src/subpath. When src is absolute, joining with base_dir does not constrain the source path, allowing artifact copies from outside the intended sandbox directory.
signals.review_reason: Same root cause (path validation not applied to absolute paths) affects LocalFile/LocalDir and GitRepo; potential arbitrary file read outside sandbox boundary. Count=2 confirms repeated pattern.

source_issues.title: LocalFile and LocalDir absolute src paths can read outside base_dir

signals.review_reason: Two separate MCP config validation failures; both silently disable safety controls for sensitive/destructive MCP tools. Misspellings in tool_filter and require_approval go undetected. Count=2 confirms this is a known pattern.

signals.summary: RunState.to_string() crashes when guardrail payloads contain datetime or other non-JSON-native values. _serialize_guardrail_results() and _serialize_tool_guardrail_results() write non-normalized values, blocking any agent using guardrails with datetime objects.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking bug with clear repro: RunState.to_string() raises TypeError on datetime guardrail payloads. Prevents any user relying on guardrail state persistence or serialization.

source_issues.evidence: RunState.to_string() crashes with TypeError when guardrail outputInfo contains datetime objects. Main flow blocking for any agent using guardrails with non-JSON-native values.

signals.topic: Streaming tool_call delta accumulation drops/mismerges fragments causing unparseable JSON
signals.summary: When streaming chunks contain multiple tool_call entries at the same index (common with speculative decoding), accumulate_delta stores them as separate list elements instead of merging, resulting in fragmented function.arguments that cannot be parsed as valid JSON.
aliases: streaming tool_calls duplicate index merge failure
tool call arguments JSON parse error streaming
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports (count=2) confirm the same root cause in accumulate_delta: duplicate-index tool_call entries in streaming chunks are stored as separate list elements instead of merged by logical index, causing function.arguments to be unparseable JSON and breaking any user relying on streaming tool calls with speculative-decoding-compatible providers. This is a clear workflow-level failure that silently corrupts tool call data.

source_issues.title: `accumulate_delta` drops tool_call fragments when one chunk has multiple entries at the same `index`
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows arguments become ': "London"}' (missing prefix) with orphaned second entry. Causes json.JSONDecodeError. Same bug in _assistants.py. Confirmed against vLLM with speculative decoding.

source_issues.title: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate indexes in first chunk are accumulated incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows two index:0 entries produced in first chunk, later chunks merge into [0] leaving second entry stranded. Final arguments are invalid JSON. Confirmed against vLLM + Kimi 2.6 speculative decoding.

signals.topic: ResponseFunctionWebSearch type definition allows action=None but accessing .action.type causes runtime AttributeError
signals.summary: The SDK type definition for ResponseFunctionWebSearch implies action cannot be None, but the API returns action=None for some web search calls. User code that safely accesses item.action.type raises AttributeError at runtime.
signals.review_reason: Single confirmed crash with explicit reproduction code: accessing .action.type on ResponseFunctionWebSearch raises AttributeError because the API returns action=None for some web search calls while the SDK type definition implies it is non-nullable. This breaks user code that safely assumes the structure matches the types, and the fix requires a type-level correction to the SDK.

source_issues.title: ResponseFunctionWebSearch doesn't match returned payload
source_issues.evidence: Author provides exact reproduction: code accessing item.action.type raises AttributeError because action=None. Specifically: sum(1 for item in raw_response.output if item.type == 'web_search_call' and item.action.type == 'search') crashes. Four web searches observed, two with action=None.

signals.topic: Responses stream accumulator crashes with AttributeError when event item is None
signals.summary: The Responses streaming accumulator assumes event.item is always present for response.output_item.added events and dereferences event.item.type directly, causing a hard crash when OpenAI-compatible providers emit item=null.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed hard crash (AttributeError) in the SDK's streaming accumulator triggered by a null item field, with full stack trace and production occurrence against an OpenAI-compatible provider. The crash occurs inside the SDK before application code can handle it, making this a blocking failure for anyone using Responses streaming with non-OpenAI backends.

source_issues.title: Responses stream accumulator crashes when response.output_item.added has item=None
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace provided: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'type' in openai/lib/streaming/responses/_responses.py accumulator. Occurred in production against a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. Exception happens inside SDK before application code can recover.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely when file status stays in_progress with no error
signals.summary: upload_and_poll() has no timeout and never returns when the vector store file gets stuck in status=in_progress indefinitely on the backend, with no last_error set to indicate failure.
aliases: vector store file stuck at in_progress
signals.review_reason: Blocking main-flow hang: upload_and_poll() has no timeout and indefinitely blocks when the vector store file processing stalls on the backend, leaving the file in in_progress with no error signal. The raw file is already processed so the hang is entirely within the SDK's polling loop. This prevents any user workflow from completing.

source_issues.title: `vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll()` can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at `in_progress`
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer provided: upload_and_poll() never returns. Raw file status=processed but vector_store_file status=in_progress forever with last_error=null. Author provides explicit polling loop repro showing the stuck state persists indefinitely. No timeout mechanism in the SDK.

signals.topic: AsyncResponses parse() causes unbounded memory leak due to Pydantic TypeVar schema rebuild failure
signals.summary: Each call to responses.parse() allocates a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust objects) because TextFormatT TypeVar cannot be resolved, causing linear RSS growth and eventual OOM in long-running servers.
signals.review_reason: Memory leak with concrete root cause analysis: each parse() call allocates unbounded heavy Rust objects (SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer) due to Pydantic TypeVar rebuild failure. Long-running servers will experience linear RSS growth and eventual OOM. Flame graph evidence provided confirming the leak path.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph attached showing memory growth. Root cause identified: construct_type_unchecked with TextFormatT TypeVar causes model_rebuild to always fail (returns False), so MockCoreSchema._built_memo is never populated, allocating new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer on every parse() call. These are heavy Rust objects that accumulate without bound, causing OOM in long-running servers.

signals.topic: Session history API does not reflect live streamed assistant/tool events during active turns, blocking programmatic progress polling
signals.summary: When acpx is used as a programmatic orchestration layer, `sessions history` only shows the user prompt while the agent is actively running. Assistant messages and tool calls are absent from the session record until the turn completes, even though they are already written to the rollout JSONL log on disk. This forces orchestrators to fall back to directly parsing the rollout log instead of using the natural session history API.
aliases: sessions history incomplete during active turn
signals.review_reason: This blocks programmatic orchestration use cases. The session history API is the intended interface for polling live progress, but it only returns user prompts during active turns, forcing users to fall back to parsing raw rollout logs. This is a UX/workflow regression introduced after the prompt-checkpoint fix in #157. Count=1 (single repo dataset), but the issue is well-documented with clear user impact and a specific reproducible scenario.

source_issues.title: ACP session history only records prompts while Codex is running
source_issues.evidence: Only user prompt shown in sessions history during active turn; rollout log has full data; orchestrator forced to parse rollout log directly instead of using sessions history API

Direct acpx claude works fine, isolating the failure to the OpenClaw spawn mechanism. The automatic two-agent ACP flow (Codex + Claude) is blocked, which is the core value proposition of the OpenClaw orchestrator. Users must fall back to Codex ACP + manual Claude review as a workaround.

signals.topic: Runtime config options (thinking/effort, timeoutSeconds) cause Claude ACP to fail, limiting usability beyond basic prompts
signals.summary: Claude Code via ACP/acpx works for clean prompts and model overrides, but fails when OpenClaw applies standard runtime controls like `timeoutSeconds` and `thinking`. Config option keys are forwarded to the Claude ACP adapter without validation against advertised options, causing ACP_TURN_FAILED / Internal error. This forces users to restrict Claude Code to basic prompts with no runtime control.
signals.review_reason: This limits Claude Code's usability to only clean prompts and model-only overrides. Any standard runtime control (thinking effort, timeout) causes a hard failure. The root cause is that config option keys (thinking, timeoutSeconds) are forwarded to the Claude ACP adapter without being validated against what the adapter advertises, surfacing as a generic internal error. Users cannot use Claude Code through OpenClaw/acpx for any non-trivial task that requires timeout or reasoning effort control.

signals.topic: WSL local gateway onboarding: validation isolation corruption and operator pairing failures
signals.summary: The WSL gateway onboarding flow (PR #274) has multiple blocking issues: (1) the validation harness writes to real user settings files instead of isolated run directories, contaminating real credentials; (2) stale tray executable is launched instead of the freshly built one, producing misleading diagnostics; (3) operator pairing fails with 'operator_auth_failed' after gateway starts, likely due to credential contamination; (4) subprocess diagnostics echo gateway tokens into logs/UI without redaction, creating token-leak risk; (5) wsl.conf section-aware validation is too loose and can misreport config state; (6) user cancellation does not terminate in-flight WSL processes, leaving orphaned work.
signals.review_reason: This is a multi-faceted onboarding blocker: the WSL gateway setup flow (a major new feature) is completely blocked — the validation harness corrupts real user credentials, operator pairing fails, tokens leak into diagnostics, and cancellation leaves orphaned processes. The monthly Repo Assist report confirms this is actively blocking PR merge. While count=1, the review_reason provides strong user-impact evidence justifying P1.

source_issues.title: WSL local gateway onboarding validation blockers from PR #274
source_issues.evidence: Issue filed by human (shanselman) after full local WSL validation run reached operator pairing and failed with 'operator_auth_failed'. Real user settings were contaminated. Multiple distinct failure modes documented — each blocks the entire WSL onboarding path. PR #274 is kept out of merge until fixes land.

signals.topic: Gateway child process orphaning blocks systemd service restarts with EADDRINUSE, causing extended downtime

signals.review_reason: This causes a full service outage loop that cannot self-heal. After a systemd restart attempt, the service permanently fails until manual intervention. This is a production deployment blocker that directly results in extended downtime, qualifying it as P1 despite count=1 due to the severe operational impact (service becomes completely unavailable and unrecoverable without manual PID cleanup).

signals.topic: vLLM-served Qwen3 reasoning traces silently dropped due to field name mismatch (`reasoning` vs `reasoning_content`)
signals.summary: When using LlamaIndex's OpenAI-compatible LLM client with vLLM serving Qwen3 reasoning models, the model's entire reasoning trace is silently discarded because `from_openai_message` only checks `reasoning_content` while vLLM exposes it as `reasoning`. This causes `ThinkingBlock` to never be appended, making reasoning invisible to downstream agents, workflows, and evaluators. The bug is silent — users assume the model isn't reasoning when the trace is being discarded at the conversion layer. Workaround requires subclassing `OpenAILike` or monkey-patching, which is fragile across upgrades.
aliases: ThinkingBlock silently dropped for vLLM Qwen3
reasoning_content field not recognized by vLLM
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow silent data-loss bug in a very common integration stack (LlamaIndex + vLLM + Qwen3). The user's entire reasoning trace — which the model generated and is present in the raw response — is silently discarded at the conversion layer, making the model appear non-reasoning to all downstream components. This is blocking for any agentic or evaluative workflow relying on ThinkingBlock, and the only workaround (subclassing/monkey-patching) is fragile. Confidence is high because the reproduction is verified with actual output showing `ThinkingBlocks found: 0` vs expected `1`.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: from_openai_message misses vLLM-served Qwen3 reasoning field (uses 'reasoning' instead of 'reasoning_content')
source_issues.evidence: Verified reproduction: vLLM response contains `reasoning` field but `from_openai_message` only reads `reasoning_content`, resulting in 0 ThinkingBlocks instead of 1. Raw response confirms the field is present. Downstream components (workflows, agents, evaluators) receive empty reasoning. Workaround requires monkey-patching which breaks on upgrades.

signals.topic: Bedrock Converse streaming produces `tool_kwargs` as JSON string instead of dict, causing Pydantic ValidationError in cross-provider workflows
signals.summary: The Bedrock Converse adapter's streaming methods construct `ToolCallBlock` objects with `tool_kwargs` as a raw JSON string rather than a parsed dict. This causes `pydantic_core.ValidationError` when other adapters (e.g., Google GenAI) consume these blocks, as they cast `tool_kwargs` to `Dict` expecting a dict type. Any workflow that persists chat history from a Bedrock streaming session and replays it through a different provider will fail. The non-streaming path works correctly because boto3 deserializes it automatically.
aliases: Bedrock Converse streaming ToolCallBlock type error
tool_kwargs string instead of dict in streaming
signals.review_reason: This causes a hard validation error (`pydantic_core.ValidationError`) that crashes workflows any time a Bedrock streaming session's chat history is consumed by another provider. The bug is well-localized (6 specific code locations in streaming paths) and the impact is clear: cross-provider RAG/agent workflows fail deterministically. The fact that the adapter's own defensive code already handles string tool_kwargs confirms the developers knew strings could appear but never fixed the root cause.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Bedrock Converse streaming produces string `tool_kwargs` in `ToolCallBlock` instead of dict
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified at 6 locations in base.py (lines 593, 649, 693, 877, 933, 978) in streaming code paths. Accumulated JSON string passed directly to ToolCallBlock without parsing. Google GenAI adapter throws `pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for FunctionCall — args — Input should be a valid dictionary [type=dict_type, input_value='{"document_id": "..."}', input_type=str]`. All cross-provider workflows with Bedrock streaming history are blocked.

signals.topic: ContextVar not propagated on non-async FunctionTool execution, breaking OpenTelemetry tracing
signals.summary: When reading `ContextVar`s within `FunctionTool`s, the values may be incorrect depending on whether the tool uses `async_fn` or `fn`. The `async_fn` path correctly propagates ContextVars, but the `fn` (sync) path does not. This is caused by LlamaIndex's custom event loop handling for non-async tool calls. The practical impact is severe for OpenTelemetry users: all non-async tool call spans appear as orphans because OpenTelemetry uses a ContextVar to correctly parent spans. Users who don't own the ContextVar (e.g., from another package like OpenTelemetry) cannot work around this issue.
aliases: Python contextvars not propagated in non-async tool execution
OpenTelemetry spans orphaned in sync tools
signals.review_reason: This breaks observability in a way that is invisible to most users until they try to debug or trace their agent runs. For OpenTelemetry users specifically, it causes complete tracing failure (orphaned spans) for all non-async tool calls — which are extremely common in production agent code. The workaround is unavailable for third-party ContextVar owners, making this a structural limitation. This qualifies as a key functionality issue (tool execution correctness) with clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `ContextVar` not propagated on non-`async` tool execution.
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced with a unit test showing async_fn tools read correct ContextVar values while sync fn tools read default values. Root cause traced to custom event loop iteration in function_tool.py lines 78-80. OpenTelemetry users are specifically affected: all non-async tool spans appear as orphans with no parent span. Users cannot work around this when ContextVars are owned by third-party packages like OpenTelemetry.

signals.topic: Deprecated `huggingface-hub[inference]` extra in embeddings-huggingface package causes dependency resolver warnings
signals.summary: `llama-index-embeddings-huggingface==0.6.1` declares `huggingface-hub[inference]>=0.19.0` as a dependency, but the `[inference]` extra was removed in huggingface-hub v1.x. The functionality was folded into the core package. This causes strict dependency resolvers (e.g., `uv sync`) to emit a warning on every install, flagging the invalid extra.
aliases: huggingface-hub inference extra removed but still declared
signals.review_reason: While this is a low-severity issue (warning only, not a hard failure), it is a confirmed user-facing problem that causes confusion with common tooling (uv, pip) and flags an invalid dependency spec. The fix is a one-character change but it represents a real packaging quality issue that users encounter on every install. The functionality loss is minimal (inference client is now in core huggingface-hub), but the warning noise is a genuine annoyance.

source_issues.title: llama-index-embeddings-huggingface: references removed `huggingface-hub[inference]` extra
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed: `uv sync` emits `warning: The package huggingface-hub==1.13.0 does not have an extra named 'inference'`. The fix is trivial (remove `[inference]` from the dependency string). The warning causes confusion and is flagged by strict dependency resolvers.

signals.topic: Encoding error when loading persisted storage_context locally (UTF-8 decode failure)
signals.summary: When loading a persisted `storage_context` from disk via `StorageContext.from_defaults(persist_dir=...)`, users encounter a `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xbd in position 48: invalid start byte`. This occurs because the storage persistence layer writes files (possibly vector store data or metadata) with an encoding that is not valid UTF-8, and the loading path assumes UTF-8. This blocks the core workflow of persisting and reloading index state.
aliases: UTF-8 decode error on storage_context recovery
signals.review_reason: This blocks the core persistence and recovery workflow of LlamaIndex — users cannot reload their saved index state. While the issue was eventually closed (and presumably fixed), its presence in a recently-active dataset suggests it may still be affecting users on older versions or in specific edge cases. The 26-comment thread confirms it is not an isolated incident. The error is a hard startup crash (UnicodeDecodeError) that prevents data recovery.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Encoding error when local loading storage_context
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced by persisting then loading storage_context: `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xbd in position 48: invalid start byte`. Issue attracted 26 comments indicating it is a real, recurring user problem affecting core persistence/recovery workflows.

signals.topic: scoped snapshot returns duplicate elements due to virtual AX nodes without backendDOMNodeId
signals.summary: When using `snapshot -i -s <selector>`, elements under the target selector appear multiple times because Chromium's AX tree contains virtual intermediate nodes (generic/group) with no backendDOMNodeId, which breaks the parent-child chain in the scoped-snapshot algorithm, incorrectly promoting child AX nodes to top-level roots and causing them to be traversed multiple times during DFS rendering.
signals.review_reason: Core snapshot command produces silently incorrect output (duplicate elements with different refs). While not a crash, it breaks automation workflows that rely on snapshot output for element identification and interaction. The bug is in the fundamental scoped-snapshot algorithm with a clear root cause. Count=1 because only one issue reports this, but the severity is high as it silently corrupts output used by downstream agents.

source_issues.title: snapshot -s <selector> produces duplicate elements when AX tree contains virtual nodes without backendDOMNodeId

The bug is in the scoped-snapshot algorithm in snapshot.rs: virtual nodes with backendDOMNodeId=None break the in_subtree chain, causing child nodes to be promoted to roots and traversed multiple times. This makes snapshot output unreliable for any automation that depends on element refs.

source_issues.evidence: User shows explicit comparison: --session flag restores login state correctly, but AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME env var does not. Also noted that the help text lists AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME twice. This breaks automated workflows that inject session names via environment variables (common in CI/CD and agent orchestration).

signals.topic: snapshot --json returns truncated accessibility tree over remote CDP WebSocket — regression from v0.25.3
signals.summary: Over remote CDP WebSocket connections (--cdp wss://...), the snapshot command returns a truncated accessibility tree (~715 chars vs ~4849 chars locally). Content inside portal-rendered components (Radix UI popovers) is missing. This breaks any workflow using snapshot output to extract interactive element refs over remote CDP, a core deployment scenario for agent services.
aliases: snapshot accessibility tree incomplete over WebSocket
snapshot --json data loss over remote CDP
signals.review_reason: Remote CDP is a core deployment scenario for agent services (headless Chrome in cloud/containerized environments). The snapshot command silently returns incomplete data — truncation means interactive elements are missing without any error message. This is a regression from a known-working version. User impact is severe for remote/cloud deployments, as element refs needed for automation are absent from output.

source_issues.title: snapshot --json returns truncated accessibility tree over remote CDP WebSocket
source_issues.evidence: Remote CDP (wss://) produces ~715 char snapshot vs ~4849 char locally. Interactive elements inside popovers (radios, combobox, tabs) are completely missing. Explicitly noted as a regression from v0.19.0 where this worked correctly. Any automation filtering refs by role returns 0 results from the truncated output, causing automated steps to fail.

signals.topic: Chrome Helper subprocesses (GPU/Renderer) not cleaned up when agent session is killed
signals.summary: When agent-browser's parent process is killed (SIGKILL, timeout, or orchestrator termination), Chrome Helper GPU and Renderer processes survive as orphans consuming ~100% CPU each. They persist until Chrome's watchdog reaps them (minutes later), causing significant battery/thermal impact and resource leaks on shared systems.
aliases: Chrome subprocess not terminated on agent exit
GPU/Renderer process leak on session kill
signals.review_reason: Chrome subprocess orphaning causes resource leaks in agent orchestration environments. Multiple CPU cores consumed per dead session, with no automatic cleanup mechanism. This is particularly impactful for agent runners handling multiple sessions — each abnormal termination leaves persistent resource consumption. The workaround requires manual intervention, which is not viable in automated environments.

source_issues.title: Chrome Helper processes (GPU/Renderer) not cleaned up when agent session is killed or times out
source_issues.evidence: Observed on macOS arm64: GPU Helper at ~100% CPU, two Renderer Helpers at ~100% CPU each (~300% total) survive SIGKILL on the parent agent process. These persist for several minutes. No post-mortem cleanup possible because the CLI process is already gone. Explicitly impacts AI agent runners (OpenClaw) in production. Suggested fixes: process group isolation or sidecar daemon for orphan monitoring.

signals.topic: Zod v4 breaking change: `z.unknown()` now requires explicit key presence, breaking all Bedrock tool calls under Zod >= 4.4.0
signals.summary: BedrockToolUseSchema declares `input: z.unknown()` which Zod v4 now requires to be present. Bedrock's Converse Stream never sends `input` on `contentBlockStart` events (args arrive via `contentBlockDelta`), causing every tool call to throw `AI_TypeValidationError` for any project running Zod >= 4.4.0. The only workarounds are pinning Zod to ^4.3.x or applying patch-package.
signals.review_reason: User-impacting: every tool call through @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock is blocked (AI_TypeValidationError) when Zod >= 4.4.0 is installed. This surfaces automatically on any routine pnpm update that pulls Zod 4.4.x. No published version of @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock survives Zod >= 4.4.0.

source_issues.title: `BedrockToolUseSchema` rejects valid `contentBlockStart` events under Zod >= 4.4.0
source_issues.evidence: Every tool call via @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock throws AI_TypeValidationError for projects running Zod >= 4.4.0. Reproduction: any tool invocation triggers 'Invalid input: expected nonoptional, received undefined' on the input field of contentBlockStart. Workaround: pin zod to ^4.3.x — not a real fix.

signals.topic: Zod v4 breaking change: `CallToolResultSchema` rejects `resource_link` content parts with Zod >= 4.4.x, breaking MCP tool results
signals.summary: CallToolResultSchema in @ai-sdk/mcp only allows text/image/embedded-resource content parts. The MCP spec defines a fourth variant, resource_link. With Zod ~4.3.6 it was tolerated; with Zod >= 4.4.1 it is hard-rejected, causing `callTool()` to throw 'Failed to parse server response'. The peer-dep range `^3.25.76 || ^4.1.8` permits 4.4.x, so this surfaces on a routine pnpm update.
signals.review_reason: User-impacting: every tool result containing a resource_link part from an MCP server is blocked (parse failure) when Zod >= 4.4.x is installed. Breaks core MCP tool-calling functionality. Root cause is identical to #14892 — same Zod v4 change requiring explicit optional markers.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/mcp: CallToolResultSchema rejects resource_link content parts with zod >= 4.4.x
source_issues.evidence: When any MCP server returns a resource_link content part in a tool result, callTool() throws 'Failed to parse server response' on Zod >= 4.4.x. Zod 4.3.x tolerated the missing union arm. peerDeps allow 4.4.x so this breaks on routine dependency update.

signals.topic: Google provider streaming parser drops complete no-args function calls, breaking multi-turn conversations on Gemini 3 thinking models
signals.summary: When `streamFunctionCallArguments: true` is set, the Google streaming parser classifies each function-call chunk into three buckets (streaming, terminal, complete). A no-args complete call arrives as `{ name: 'X' }` and matches none of the three classifiers, causing it to be silently dropped. This also drops the `thoughtSignature` that Gemini 3 requires on all tool-call-bearing turns. Vertex enforces 'must have thoughtSignature' on multi-turn; the next step 400s. The bug also exists in AI Gateway's server-side parser.
aliases: Google streaming parser drops no-args function calls
signals.review_reason: P0 despite count=1 due to critical severity: ~50% of all multi-turn Gemini 3 conversations fail in production. The bug silently drops the entire first function call AND its required thoughtSignature, causing Vertex to reject the next agent step with a 400. No viable user workaround without changing tool API contracts.

source_issues.title: `@ai-sdk/google` streaming parser drops no-args function calls, losing `thoughtSignature`
source_issues.evidence: Wire capture shows Vertex sends the thoughtSignature on the first call chunk. Parser drops it because `{ name: 'X' }` matches no classifier bucket. ~50% of multi-turn continuations fail (correlates with whether model picks the no-args tool first). Vertex 400s next step with 'missing thought_signature'. No real workaround — adding required args changes API contract and optional args are still omitted by the model.

signals.topic: `addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema` forcibly adds `additionalProperties: false`, which xAI/Grok API explicitly rejects, completely breaking tool calling
signals.summary: The addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema utility unconditionally sets `additionalProperties: false` on all object schemas during tool serialization. xAI's validator explicitly rejects `additionalProperties: false` because xAI defaults to that behavior already. Every tool call to xAI/Grok models fails with 'Schema validation failed: property schema false is not supported'. Workaround is to disable tool calling entirely for xAI models.
signals.review_reason: User-impacting: tool calling is completely non-functional for all xAI/Grok model users. The only workaround is disabling tool calling entirely, which removes a key feature. xAI is a supported provider; this blocks a primary use case.

source_issues.title: addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema breaks xAI/Grok tool calling: xAI rejects additionalProperties: false
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed in production and via investigation: xAI rejects schemas with additionalProperties: false. The SDK re-adds this even after application-level sanitization. The only workaround is disabling tool calling entirely for xAI models.

signals.topic: Anthropic provider auto-injects obsolete `effort-2025-11-24` beta header, causing all effort-using requests to 400 on Vertex AI
signals.summary: When `providerOptions.anthropic.effort` is set, @ai-sdk/anthropic auto-injects the `anthropic-beta: effort-2025-11-24` header. The effort feature went GA on 2025-11-24 with no beta header required; only the `output_config.effort` body field is needed. Vertex AI now strictly validates this header and rejects it with HTTP 400. Every effort-using request through `createVertexAnthropic` fails. The body field works fine — only the header is wrong.
aliases: obsolete effort beta header Vertex rejected
signals.review_reason: User-impacting: every effort-based request through createVertexAnthropic returns HTTP 400 and fails. Users who need per-request effort control on Vertex cannot use the feature. The body field works; the workarounds (using direct Anthropic, not using effort) both sacrifice desired functionality.

source_issues.title: fix(provider/anthropic): stop sending obsolete effort-2025-11-24 beta header (rejected by Vertex)
source_issues.evidence: Direct reproduction confirms the SDK injects the stale header on a minimal fake-key request. End-to-end on Vertex returns 400: 'Unexpected value(s) effort-2025-11-24 for the anthropic-beta header.' Users who need per-request effort control on Vertex are blocked.

signals.topic: CLI `vercel env add --value` silently stores empty string for both sensitive and non-sensitive environment variables, causing silent production failures

In CLI 50.5.0+, the `--sensitive` flag has the same silent failure. Affected variables show as 'Encrypted' in dashboard but read as `""` at runtime, breaking HMAC verification, API keys, signing keys — often only discovered in production.
aliases: env add --value stores empty string silently
CLI env var silent empty value corruption
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 production-blocking bug: CLI silently corrupts environment variable values (both sensitive and non-sensitive) at write time, reporting success while storing empty strings. The broken values only surface at runtime in production (empty API keys, broken HMAC), making diagnosis difficult. CLI 53.x is the current npm 'latest', meaning all new npm installs of `vercel` globally are affected. The --sensitive regression has been live since 50.5.0 (~3+ months). The silent failure with misleading 'Added Environment Variable' success output is the core user harm.

source_issues.title: vercel env add: --value silently stored as empty string (CLI 53.x), and --sensitive empty since 50.5.0

CLI 50.5.0+ silently empties --sensitive writes. `vercel env pull` returns NAME="" for affected variables. CLI prints 'Added Environment Variable' success message even when value is empty. Breaks HMAC verification and API keys silently in production.

signals.topic: Prerender Functions do not forward URL query parameters, breaking ISR and dynamic routing use cases

signals.topic: Skew Protection is not enforced for Node.js runtime routes in @vercel/react-router, silently disabling deployment safety feature
signals.summary: The @vercel/react-router Vite plugin only injects the Skew Protection entry server (which sets the __vdpl cookie) for edge runtime routes. Node.js runtime routes fall back to React Router's default entry.server, which has no skew protection. Users who enable Skew Protection in the dashboard are silently unprotected on Node.js routes, leading to 404s on cached HTML assets after each deploy.
aliases: Skew Protection __vdpl cookie not set for nodejs routes
signals.review_reason: A deployment safety feature (Skew Protection) is silently disabled for the default Node.js runtime in @vercel/react-router. Users who explicitly enable skew protection in the dashboard believe they are protected, but the protection is completely absent for nodejs routes. The symptom (404s on cached assets post-deploy) directly blocks users from deploying safely.

source_issues.title: @vercel/react-router: Skew Protection entry.server only injected for edge runtime, not nodejs
source_issues.evidence: Skew Protection is enabled in dashboard but __vdpl cookie is never set for nodejs runtime routes. curl -sI on a nodejs deployment URL shows no Set-Cookie: __vdpl header. After each deploy, clients with cached HTML get 404s for old content-hashed asset chunks. The Vercel entry server with skew protection is only injected for edge runtime.

signals.summary: Storybook/Chromatic MCP OAuth fails because Zed's client metadata declares http://127.0.0.1/callback but Zed sends a dynamic port URI http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback which Chromatic rejects
signals.review_reason: OAuth authentication for third-party MCP integrations is completely broken due to a redirect URI mismatch. Zed sends a dynamic port in the callback URL which third-party providers reject. This blocks users from connecting Storybook/Chromatic MCP to Zed — a key integration use case. Explicit protocol violation with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Storybook/Chromatic MCP OAuth redirect URI mismatch
source_issues.evidence: OAuth redirect_uri not registered in client metadata document. Zed client metadata at zed.dev/oauth/client-metadata.json declares 'http://127.0.0.1/callback' but Zed sends 'http://127.0.0.1:<dynamic-port>/callback'. Chromatic rejects the mismatch.

signals.topic: LSP Go-To-Definition and Hover sends hundreds of duplicate requests for same position
signals.summary: Holding Ctrl and moving mouse over code sends an LSP request for every mouse event even when cursor is on the same position, creating hundreds of duplicate requests and degrading IDE performance
signals.review_reason: LSP is Zed's core code intelligence infrastructure. Hover and Go-To-Definition sending hundreds of duplicate requests per position causes measurable performance degradation and wastes LSP server resources. This affects every user actively navigating code, representing a significant UX regression.

source_issues.title: Go-To Definition and Hover is spamming LSP
source_issues.evidence: Holding CTRL and moving mouse over code fires LSP request for every mouse event even when cursor is on the same position. Results in hundreds of duplicate requests for the same position visible in LSP log. Also fires repeatedly for positions that return null hover response.

signals.topic: File encoding not detected for XML files, causing content to display as garbled text
signals.summary: Opening XML files with iso-8859-15 encoding causes Zed to mis-detect encoding as windows-1252, displaying the euro sign as a replacement symbol
signals.review_reason: File encoding misdetection causes content to render incorrectly (euro sign shown as replacement symbol). While not a crash, this represents silent data corruption in the editor — users may not notice wrong characters, potentially causing bugs in their code. A concrete, reproducible display bug with clear expected vs actual behavior.

source_issues.title: File encoding not detected when opening XML files
source_issues.evidence: User reports XML file with iso-8859-15 encoding displays 'Test ¤ sign' instead of 'Test € sign'. Zed status bar shows 'windows-1252 (current)' instead of 'iso-8859-15'. Encoding selector confirms wrong detection.
